e.en: The {kite-flyer} waited for a stronger wind.
e.zh: 放风筝的人等着更大的风。

e.en: Every {kite-flyer} on the beach looked upward.
e.zh: 海滩上的每个放风筝的人都抬头望着天空。

e.en: We went {kite-flying} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后我们去放风筝。

e.en: {Kite-flying} is popular in the park each spring.
e.zh: 每年春天，公园里都很流行放风筝。

e.en: The helmet carries a British {kite-mark}.
e.zh: 这顶头盔带有英国质量认证标志。

e.en: Look for the {kite-mark} before buying the plug.
e.zh: 购买插头前要看有没有英国质量认证标志。

e.en: He learned {kiteboarding} on a windy beach.
e.zh: 他在一个多风的海滩学会了风筝冲浪。

e.en: Strong currents can make {kiteboarding} dangerous.
e.zh: 强水流会让风筝冲浪变得危险。

e.en: The museum displayed a preserved {kitefish}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一条保存下来的风筝鱼标本。

e.en: A {kitefish} glided close to the seabed.
e.zh: 一条鳐类鱼贴近海床滑行。

e.en: The children enjoyed {kiteflying} in the field.
e.zh: 孩子们在田野里开心地放风筝。

e.en: Good weather made {kiteflying} easy that afternoon.
e.zh: 那天下午天气很好，放风筝很轻松。

e.en: The bird had a {kitelike} silhouette against the sun.
e.zh: 那只鸟在阳光下呈现出风筝般的轮廓。

e.en: A {kitelike} frame supported the experimental wing.
e.zh: 一个风筝状框架支撑着那片实验机翼。

e.en: The team launched a {kitemeteorograph} before the storm.
e.zh: 团队在暴风雨前放飞了一台风筝气象记录仪。

e.en: Data from the {kitemeteorograph} showed rising humidity.
e.zh: 风筝气象记录仪的数据表明湿度在上升。

e.en: She wore a bright {kitenge} to the wedding.
e.zh: 她穿着一块鲜艳的东非彩印布去参加婚礼。

e.en: The market sells shirts made from {kitenge}.
e.zh: 市场出售用东非彩印布做的衬衫。

e.en: The musician played a reconstructed {kithara}.
e.zh: 那位音乐家演奏了一把复原的古希腊七弦琴。

e.en: Images of the {kithara} appear on ancient pottery.
e.zh: 古代陶器上出现了古希腊七弦琴的图像。

kirksite.t: 一种含汞矿物，柯克石英

e.en: The mineralogist identified the sample as {kirksite} after several tests.
e.zh: 矿物学家经过几项测试后认定样本是柯克石英。

e.en: A small vein of {kirksite} appeared in the old mine report.
e.zh: 旧矿山报告中提到发现了一小脉柯克石英。

e.en: The church held a {kirmess} to raise money for repairs.
e.zh: 教堂举办了一场慈善游园会，为修缮筹款。

e.en: Children danced in costume at the village {kirmess}.
e.zh: 孩子们穿着服装在村里的集市庆典上跳舞。

e.en: The farmers gathered for the {kirn} after the last field was cut.
e.zh: 最后一块田收割完后，农民们聚在一起庆祝丰收节。

e.en: Songs and ale marked the old Scottish {kirn}.
e.zh: 歌声和麦酒是古老苏格兰收割庆宴的标志。

e.en: A baptized Sikh may wear a {kirpan} as an article of faith.
e.zh: 受戒的锡克教徒可能会佩戴短剑，作为信仰标志。

e.en: The school discussed how to accommodate the student's {kirpan}.
e.zh: 学校讨论了如何接纳这名学生佩戴的锡克教短剑。

e.en: The doctor noted mild {kirrhonosis} in the patient's chart.
e.zh: 医生在病历中记录了患者有轻微皮肤发黄。

e.en: Severe liver disease can sometimes cause {kirrhonosis}.
e.zh: 严重肝病有时会导致皮肤发黄。

e.en: The meteorite contained tiny crystals of {kirschsteinite}.
e.zh: 这块陨石含有微小的钙铁橄榄石晶体。

e.en: Researchers heated the sample until {kirschsteinite} began to form.
e.zh: 研究人员加热样本，直到钙铁橄榄石开始形成。

e.en: She flavored the dessert with a splash of {kirschwasser}.
e.zh: 她往甜点里加了一点樱桃白兰地调味。

e.en: The bartender served chilled {kirschwasser} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后，酒保端上了冰镇樱桃白兰地。

e.en: The paper described {kisantamine} as one compound isolated from the plant.
e.zh: 论文把基桑塔明描述为从该植物中分离出的一种化合物。

e.en: Few pharmacologists have studied {kisantamine} in detail.
e.zh: 很少有药理学家详细研究过基桑塔明。

e.en: Chemists reported traces of {kisantine} in the root extract.
e.zh: 化学家报告称根部提取物中有微量基桑廷。

e.en: The structure of {kisantine} was compared with related alkaloids.
e.zh: 研究人员将基桑廷的结构与相关生物碱作了比较。

e.en: The collection included a labeled specimen of {kischtomite}.
e.zh: 这批藏品中有一件标注为基什托石的标本。

e.en: Only specialists were familiar with {kischtomite} and its properties.
e.zh: 只有专业人士熟悉基什托石及其性质。

e.en: The foundry workers skimmed {kish} from the molten iron.
e.zh: 铸造厂工人从铁水表面撇去了石墨浮渣。

e.en: Fine flakes of {kish} can form during ironmaking.
e.zh: 炼铁过程中可能形成细小的石墨浮片。

e.en: Grandmother served hot {kishka} with potatoes and gravy.
e.zh: 祖母端上热腾腾的东欧灌肠，配着土豆和肉汁。

e.en: The deli sells {kishka} made with buckwheat and spices.
e.zh: 这家熟食店出售用荞麦和香料做的填馅肠。

e.en: He ordered {kishke} from the old Jewish deli.
e.zh: 他在那家老犹太熟食店点了东欧填馅肠。

e.en: The recipe stuffs the {kishke} with flour, fat, and onions.
e.zh: 这个食谱用面粉、油脂和洋葱来填制这种灌肠。

e.en: The actor denied writing a {kiss-and-tell} memoir about his marriage.
e.zh: 那位演员否认写过一本曝光婚姻私情的回忆录。

e.en: Editors paid well for {kiss-and-tell} stories in the tabloids.
e.zh: 小报编辑愿意为爆料艳史的故事支付高价。

e.en: Nobody trusted the office {kiss-ass} after the promotion meeting.
e.zh: 晋升会议后，没人信任办公室里那个拍马屁的人。

e.en: Stop trying to {kiss-ass} and just do the work.
e.zh: 别再拍马屁了，踏实把工作做完。

e.en: A neat {kiss-curl} rested on her forehead.
e.zh: 她额前垂着一缕整齐的小卷发。

e.en: The stylist shaped a single {kiss-curl} above his eyebrow.
e.zh: 发型师在他眉毛上方做出一缕小卷发。

e.en: The children played {kiss-in-the-ring} at the village party.
e.zh: 孩子们在村里的聚会上玩围圈亲吻游戏。

e.en: Old books mention {kiss-in-the-ring} as a courtship game.
e.zh: 旧书把围圈亲吻游戏说成一种求爱游戏。

e.en: She whispered, "{Kiss-me}," before the train arrived.
e.zh: 火车到站前，她低声说：“吻我。”

e.en: The note simply said {kiss-me} in red ink.
e.zh: 纸条上只是用红墨水写着“吻我”。

kiss-me-quick.t: 廉价艳俗的度假纪念品

e.en: He bought a {kiss-me-quick} hat at the seaside stall.
e.zh: 他在海边摊位买了一顶写着调情字样的廉价帽子。

e.en: The shop window was full of {kiss-me-quick} souvenirs.
e.zh: 商店橱窗里摆满了廉价艳俗的度假纪念品。

e.en: The lifeguard gave him the {kiss-of-life} on the beach.
e.zh: 救生员在海滩上给他做了人工呼吸。

e.en: The new funding was the {kiss-of-life} for the failing project.
e.zh: 这笔新资金成了那个濒危项目的救命转机。

e.en: Her short email was a polite {kiss-off}.
e.zh: 她那封简短邮件是一次客气的拒绝。

e.en: The manager tried to {kiss-off} the complaint with a voucher.
e.zh: 经理试图用一张代金券把投诉打发掉。

e.en: The baby had soft, {kissable} cheeks.
e.zh: 宝宝的脸颊柔软可爱，让人想亲。

e.en: The lipstick promised smooth, {kissable} lips all evening.
e.zh: 这款口红号称能让双唇整晚柔滑诱人。

e.en: Her lips looked {kissably} soft in the candlelight.
e.zh: 烛光下，她的嘴唇看起来柔软得令人想亲。

e.en: The ad described the balm as making skin {kissably} smooth.
e.zh: 广告说这款润肤膏能让皮肤变得柔滑诱人。

e.en: The documentary interviewed former {Klansmen} about the group's violence.
e.zh: 这部纪录片采访了前三K党成员，讲述该组织的暴力行为。

e.en: Several {klansmen} gathered to settle the dispute within the clan.
e.zh: 几名氏族成员聚在一起解决族内争端。

e.en: The mineralogist identified the dark sample as {klaprothite}.
e.zh: 矿物学家把这块深色样本鉴定为硫铋铜矿。

e.en: Old catalogues listed {klaprothite} among rare copper bismuth sulfides.
e.zh: 旧目录把硫铋铜矿列在罕见的铜铋硫化物之中。

e.en: The neighbors exchanged {klatsch} over coffee every morning.
e.zh: 邻居们每天早上喝咖啡时闲聊八卦。

e.en: Her column mixed theatre news with sharp social {klatsch}.
e.zh: 她的专栏把戏剧新闻和尖刻的社交传闻混在一起。

e.en: The local {klavern} recruited members through secret meetings.
e.zh: 当地三K党分会通过秘密会议招募成员。

e.en: Police records described the {klavern} as a violent extremist cell.
e.zh: 警方记录称这个三K党地方分会是暴力极端组织小组。

e.en: A traveling {kleagle} tried to sign up new members in the county.
e.zh: 一名巡回三K党招募员试图在该县拉新成员入会。

e.en: The article exposed his past work as a {kleagle}.
e.zh: 那篇文章揭露了他过去曾担任三K党招募员。

e.en: A {klegg} bit the horse near the riverbank.
e.zh: 一只牛虻在河岸边叮了那匹马。

e.en: Farm workers hated the summer swarms of {kleggs}.
e.zh: 农场工人讨厌夏天成群出现的叮人马蝇。

e.en: Engineers tested the concrete's {klendusity} after weeks of heavy rain.
e.zh: 连续数周大雨后，工程师测试了混凝土的抗渗性。

e.en: Good brickwork depends partly on the {klendusity} of its surface.
e.zh: 优质砖砌体在一定程度上取决于表面的防水密实度。

e.en: The old ballad praised a {klepht} who resisted Ottoman rule.
e.zh: 那首古老民谣赞颂了一位反抗奥斯曼统治的希腊游击义士。

e.en: Travelers feared meeting a {klepht} in the mountain pass.
e.zh: 旅人害怕在山口遇到希腊山贼。

klephtic.t: 希腊山贼的；游击义士的

e.en: The museum displayed weapons from the {klephtic} resistance.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了希腊游击义士抵抗运动使用过的武器。

e.en: He collected {klephtic} songs from villages in the hills.
e.zh: 他从山村收集希腊山贼与义士题材的歌谣。

e.en: The movie turns the charming {klepto} into an unlikely hero.
e.zh: 这部电影把那个迷人的小偷塑造成了意想不到的英雄。

e.en: She joked that her cat was a {klepto} for stealing socks.
e.zh: 她开玩笑说，她的猫老偷袜子，简直有偷窃癖。

e.en: Critics called the regime a {kleptocracy} built on stolen public money.
e.zh: 批评者称该政权是靠盗取公款建立的贪腐统治。

e.en: The report traced how the {kleptocracy} hid assets overseas.
e.zh: 报告追踪了这个盗贼政权如何把资产藏到海外。

e.en: The exiled {kleptocrat} bought mansions with state funds.
e.zh: 那名流亡的贪腐统治者用国家资金购买豪宅。

e.en: Sanctions targeted each {kleptocrat} linked to the stolen oil revenue.
e.zh: 制裁针对每个与被盗石油收入有关的盗国者。

e.en: The psychiatrist described {kleptohemodeipnonism} as an extremely rare compulsion.
e.zh: 精神科医生称病态偷宴食癖是一种极其罕见的强迫行为。

e.en: A Victorian case note mentioned {kleptohemodeipnonism} after repeated thefts at dinners.
e.zh: 一份维多利亚时代病例记录提到，多次在宴席偷食后被诊断为病态偷宴食癖。

e.en: Her {kleptophobia} made crowded markets feel unbearable.
e.zh: 她的偷窃恐惧症让拥挤的市场变得难以忍受。

e.en: After the burglary, his {kleptophobia} grew worse at night.
e.zh: 入室盗窃事件之后，他夜里怕被偷的恐惧更严重了。

e.en: Don't stand there like a {klotz}.
e.zh: 别像个笨蛋一样站在那里。

e.en: He felt like a {klotz} after dropping the tray.
e.zh: 他把托盘摔了以后觉得自己笨手笨脚。

e.en: The old app still runs on several ugly {kludges}.
e.zh: 这个旧应用还靠几个难看的临时补丁运行。

e.en: She {kludges} a report together before every meeting.
e.zh: 她每次开会前都临时拼凑一份报告。

e.en: The interface feels {kludgey} on small screens.
e.zh: 这个界面在小屏幕上用起来很拼凑粗糙。

e.en: They accepted a {kludgey} fix until the rewrite was ready.
e.zh: 在重写完成前，他们接受了一个凑合的修复办法。

e.en: The pipe fell with a loud {klunk}.
e.zh: 管子掉下来，发出一声沉闷的撞击声。

e.en: His first car was a rusty old {klunk}.
e.zh: 他的第一辆车是一辆生锈的破旧老车。

e.en: The camera controls felt {klunky} and slow.
e.zh: 相机控制用起来很笨拙，而且反应很慢。

e.en: She wore {klunky} boots through the snow.
e.zh: 她穿着笨重的靴子在雪地里走。

e.en: The engineer studied the {klydonogram} after the surge test.
e.zh: 浪涌测试后，工程师研究了那张浪涌波形记录图。

e.en: A clear {klydonogram} can reveal insulation problems.
e.zh: 清晰的浪涌波形记录图能显示绝缘问题。

e.en: The lab calibrated the {klydonograph} before testing.
e.zh: 实验室在测试前校准了浪涌记录仪。

e.en: A {klydonograph} records sudden electrical surges.
e.zh: 浪涌记录仪会记录突发的电涌。

e.en: The radar used a powerful {klystron}.
e.zh: 那台雷达使用了一支大功率速调管。

e.en: A {klystron} can amplify microwave signals.
e.zh: 速调管可以放大微波信号。

e.en: The injured horse was taken to the {knackery}.
e.zh: 那匹受伤的马被送到了处理病老牲畜的屠宰场。

e.en: The village {knackery} also collected dead farm animals.
e.zh: 村里的病畜屠宰场也收走农场死掉的牲畜。

e.en: He grilled a {knackwurst} for lunch.
e.zh: 他午饭烤了一根德国蒜味粗香肠。

e.en: The soup came with slices of {knackwurst}.
e.zh: 这碗汤里配了几片德国粗香肠。

e.en: We ordered two {knackwursts} with mustard.
e.zh: 我们点了两根德国蒜味粗香肠，配芥末。

e.en: The butcher displayed several smoked {knackwursts}.
e.zh: 肉铺摆出了几根烟熏德国粗香肠。

e.en: It is a {knacky} little repair job.
e.zh: 这是个需要一点巧劲的小修理活。

e.en: Her {knacky} fingers fixed the clasp quickly.
e.zh: 她手指灵巧，很快修好了搭扣。

e.en: His sleeve caught on a sharp {knag}.
e.zh: 他的袖子被一个尖突的木节勾住了。

e.en: A small {knag} stuck out from the old branch.
e.zh: 老树枝上突出来一个小短节。

e.en: The {knagged} stick was hard to hold.
e.zh: 那根多节的棍子握起来很不舒服。

e.en: They walked past a {knagged} old oak.
e.zh: 他们走过一棵枝节突出的老橡树。

e.en: The table was made from {knaggy} pine.
e.zh: 这张桌子是用多木节的松木做的。

e.en: A {knaggy} path led up the hill.
e.zh: 一条崎岖粗糙的小路通向山上。

e.en: He learned to {knap} flint into arrowheads.
e.zh: 他学会了把燧石敲打成箭头。

e.en: The cottage stood on a grassy {knap}.
e.zh: 小屋坐落在一个长满草的小山顶上。

e.en: The museum displayed a {knapped} flint blade.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一把敲制成形的燧石刀片。

e.en: She {knapped} the stone with careful blows.
e.zh: 她小心敲击那块石头，使它成形。

e.en: The {knapper} shaped flint with a horn tool.
e.zh: 那名燧石敲制工用角制工具给燧石塑形。

e.en: A skilled {knapper} could make sharp stone blades.
e.zh: 熟练的敲石工能做出锋利的石刀片。

kleptoscope.t: 早期电影放映装置；窥片机

e.en: The museum displayed a working {kleptoscope} from early cinema.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一台早期电影时期还能运转的窥片机。

e.en: Visitors peered into the {kleptoscope} to watch the short scene.
e.zh: 参观者透过这台窥片机观看那段短短的画面。

e.en: The patrol walked five {kliks} before dawn.
e.zh: 巡逻队在天亮前走了五公里。

e.en: The village is only two {kliks} from here.
e.zh: 那个村子离这里只有两公里。

e.en: The glasses {klink} together at midnight.
e.zh: 午夜时分，酒杯相碰发出叮当声。

e.en: I heard the keys {klink} in his pocket.
e.zh: 我听见钥匙在他口袋里叮当作响。

e.en: The mason chose {klinkstone} for the old courtyard wall.
e.zh: 石匠为旧院墙选用了敲击会发响的硬石。

e.en: A sharp tap made the {klinkstone} ring clearly.
e.zh: 轻轻一敲，那块响石就发出清脆的声音。

klinokinesis.t: 倾向运动；刺激定向行为

e.en: The larvae showed {klinokinesis} when the light changed.
e.zh: 光线变化时，幼虫表现出倾向运动。

e.en: Researchers measured {klinokinesis} in response to chemical gradients.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了生物对化学梯度产生的倾向运动。

e.en: The worm used {klinotaxis} to move toward the odor.
e.zh: 这条虫通过摆动定向朝气味来源移动。

e.en: In {klinotaxis}, the animal samples stimuli by turning its body.
e.zh: 在趋性运动中，动物通过转动身体来感知刺激。

e.en: The old road ran below a chalk {klint}.
e.zh: 那条老路从一片白垩陡崖下方经过。

e.en: Waves slowly cut into the coastal {klint}.
e.zh: 海浪缓慢侵蚀着那片海岸断崖。

e.en: A {klipdas} warmed itself on the rock.
e.zh: 一只岩狸在石头上晒太阳取暖。

e.en: The guide pointed out a {klipdas} near the cliff.
e.zh: 向导指给我们看悬崖旁的一只蹄兔。

e.en: The {klipdassie} vanished between the stones.
e.zh: 那只岩狸消失在石缝之间。

e.en: Children watched a {klipdassie} feeding on leaves.
e.zh: 孩子们看着一只蹄兔吃树叶。

e.en: They soaked the {klipfish} overnight before cooking.
e.zh: 他们烹调前把盐干鳕鱼泡了一整夜。

e.en: The market sold imported {klipfish} in wooden boxes.
e.zh: 市场用木箱出售进口的腌干鱼。

e.en: The map marked a small {klippe} above the valley.
e.zh: 地图标出了山谷上方一处小的孤立岩块。

e.en: Geologists studied the {klippe} to trace ancient faulting.
e.zh: 地质学家研究这处飞来峰，以追踪古老断层活动。

e.en: A {klipspringer} balanced easily on the steep rocks.
e.zh: 一只岩羚轻松地站在陡峭岩石上保持平衡。

e.en: The safari group spotted a {klipspringer} at sunrise.
e.zh: 狩猎观光团在日出时看见了一只非洲岩羚。

e.en: The engineer checked the amplifier's {klirr} at high volume.
e.zh: 工程师检查了放大器在高音量下的失真系数。

e.en: Low {klirr} helps the speaker sound cleaner.
e.zh: 较低的谐波失真能让扬声器听起来更干净。

e.en: The datasheet lists the {klirrfactor} for each frequency range.
e.zh: 数据表列出了各个频段的失真系数。

e.en: A smaller {klirrfactor} usually means more accurate audio reproduction.
e.zh: 较小的总谐波失真通常意味着音频还原更准确。

e.en: She applied {klister} before skiing on wet snow.
e.zh: 她在湿雪上滑行前涂了越野滑雪用黏性蜡。

e.en: Too much {klister} made the skis drag uphill.
e.zh: 黏性蜡涂得太多，让滑雪板上坡时发涩。

e.en: The collection included a dark sample of {klockmannite}.
e.zh: 这批藏品中有一块深色的硒铜矿标本。

e.en: Miners found {klockmannite} in the selenium-rich vein.
e.zh: 矿工在富含硒的矿脉中发现了克洛克曼矿。

e.en: The artist called the sculpture a digital {klone}.
e.zh: 艺术家把这件雕塑称为一个数字克隆品。

e.en: Fans joked that the new singer was a {klone} of the star.
e.zh: 歌迷开玩笑说这位新歌手像那位明星的复制品。

e.en: Their boat turned into a narrow {klong} behind the market.
e.zh: 他们的船拐进了市场后面一条狭窄的泰国小运河。

e.en: Houses on stilts lined the quiet {klong}.
e.zh: 安静的水道两旁排列着高脚屋。

e.en: The novel uses {klooch} in a dated and offensive passage.
e.zh: 这部小说在一段过时且冒犯的文字中用了原住民女子这一旧称。

e.en: Editors added a note explaining that {klooch} is now offensive.
e.zh: 编辑加了注释，说明这个旧词如今带有冒犯性。

e.en: Mist filled the {kloof} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后雾气弥漫在那条南非峡谷里。

e.en: The trail dropped sharply into a rocky {kloof}.
e.zh: 小路陡然下降，通向一条多岩石的深沟。

e.en: The archive marked {klootchman} as an obsolete colonial term.
e.zh: 档案把这个词标注为已经废弃的殖民时期用语，指原住民女子。

e.en: Modern writers avoid {klootchman} because it is offensive.
e.zh: 现代作者避免使用这个词，因为它带有冒犯性。

e.en: The archaeologist demonstrated {knapping} with a piece of flint.
e.zh: 考古学家用一块燧石演示了敲制石器。

e.en: Careful {knapping} shaped the stone into a sharp blade.
e.zh: 细致的敲削把石头做成了一把锋利的刀片。

e.en: She {knaps} the flint until an edge appears.
e.zh: 她不断敲削燧石，直到边缘显现出来。

e.en: Low {knaps} rose beyond the wet meadow.
e.zh: 湿草地那边起伏着几座低矮的小丘。

e.en: A dark {knar} marked the old oak's trunk.
e.zh: 老橡树的树干上有一个深色树节。

e.en: The carpenter worked around the hard {knar} in the board.
e.zh: 木匠绕开木板里那块坚硬的木瘤来加工。

e.en: The walking stick had a rough {knarl} near the handle.
e.zh: 那根手杖靠近把手处有个粗糙的木瘤。

e.en: Rain collected in the {knarl} of the ancient tree.
e.zh: 雨水积在那棵古树的扭结树节里。

e.en: His {knarred} hands showed years of hard work.
e.zh: 他那双粗糙多节的手显出多年劳作的痕迹。

e.en: A {knarred} branch twisted over the path.
e.zh: 一根扭曲多节的树枝横在小路上方。

e.en: The tale lists the servant's many {knaveries}.
e.zh: 这个故事列举了那个仆人的许多欺诈行径。

e.en: His petty {knaveries} finally cost him every friend.
e.zh: 他那些卑劣的小伎俩最终让他失去了所有朋友。

e.en: The judge saw through the merchant's {knavery}.
e.zh: 法官看穿了那个商人的欺诈行为。

e.en: In old comedies, {knavery} often drives the plot.
e.zh: 在老式喜剧中，无赖行径常常推动情节发展。

e.en: He gave a {knavish} smile before hiding the coin.
e.zh: 他藏起硬币前露出一个狡诈的笑。

e.en: The play's {knavish} hero cheats everyone in town.
e.zh: 剧中那个无赖主角骗了镇上的每个人。

e.en: He {knavishly} blamed his brother for the broken vase.
e.zh: 他狡诈地把打碎花瓶的责任推给弟弟。

e.en: The rogue {knavishly} bowed while stealing the purse.
e.zh: 那个无赖一边假意鞠躬，一边偷走了钱包。

e.en: His {knavishness} made every promise sound suspicious.
e.zh: 他的狡诈无赖让每个承诺都显得可疑。

e.en: The novel treats youthful {knavishness} with dry humor.
e.zh: 这部小说用冷幽默描写年轻人的无赖恶作剧。

e.en: Tiny {knawel} grew between the stones of the path.
e.zh: 小径石缝间长着细小的匍匐草本植物。

e.en: The botanist identified the weed as {knawel}.
e.zh: 植物学家把这种杂草认定为克诺草一类的小草本。

e.en: Add water until the dough becomes {kneadable}.
e.zh: 加水直到面团变得可以揉捏。

e.en: The clay stayed soft and {kneadable} for hours.
e.zh: 这块黏土好几个小时都保持柔软，能揉成形。

e.en: The actor wore {knee-breeches} for the period drama.
e.zh: 演员在那部年代剧里穿着旧式齐膝短裤。

e.en: His portrait shows silk stockings below black {knee-breeches}.
e.zh: 他的肖像中，黑色齐膝短裤下面露出丝质长袜。

e.en: We stood {knee-deep} in snow by noon.
e.zh: 到中午时，我们站在齐膝深的雪里。

e.en: She was {knee-deep} in paperwork all week.
e.zh: 她整周都深陷一堆文书工作之中。

e.en: The garden was filled with {knee-high} weeds.
e.zh: 花园里长满了齐膝高的杂草。

e.en: I knew him when he was {knee-high} to me.
e.zh: 他还很小的时候我就认识他了。

e.en: She chose a {knee-length} coat for the interview.
e.zh: 她为面试选了一件及膝外套。

e.en: The school requires {knee-length} skirts in winter.
e.zh: 学校要求冬天穿长到膝盖的裙子。

e.en: He strapped on a {knee-pad} before skating.
e.zh: 滑冰前他绑上了一个护膝垫。

e.en: The worker replaced a torn {knee-pad}.
e.zh: 那名工人换掉了一个破损的护膝垫。

e.en: Grandpa told a {knee-slapper} at dinner.
e.zh: 爷爷在晚饭时讲了一个令人捧腹的笑话。

e.en: The joke was no {knee-slapper}, but people smiled.
e.zh: 那个笑话算不上特别好笑，但大家还是笑了。

e.en: The old horse looked {knee-sprung} after years of work.
e.zh: 那匹老马多年劳作后显得前膝弯曲。

e.en: A {knee-sprung} gelding may stumble on rough ground.
e.zh: 前膝弯曲的阉马在崎岖地面上可能会绊倒。

e.en: The museum displayed velvet {kneebreeches} from the eighteenth century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了十八世纪的天鹅绒齐膝短裤。

e.en: He appeared onstage in powdered hair and {kneebreeches}.
e.zh: 他戴着扑粉假发、穿着旧式马裤登上舞台。

e.en: The insect's {kneebrush} helped it carry pollen.
e.zh: 这种昆虫腿上的毛刷状结构帮助它携带花粉。

e.en: Under the lens, the {kneebrush} looked like fine combs.
e.zh: 在镜头下，那处腿部刷毛看起来像细小的梳子。

e.en: The antique desk had a narrow {kneehole}.
e.zh: 那张古董书桌下面有个狭窄的容膝空档。

e.en: He pulled the chair closer to the {kneehole}.
e.zh: 他把椅子拉近桌下放膝盖的空档。

e.en: Students held a {kneel-in} outside the church.
e.zh: 学生们在教堂外举行了跪地抗议。

e.en: The peaceful {kneel-in} lasted through the afternoon.
e.zh: 这场和平的跪祷示威持续了整个下午。

e.en: Wear a {kneepad} when you scrub the floor.
e.zh: 擦地板时戴上护膝。

e.en: Her volleyball {kneepad} softened the fall.
e.zh: 她的排球护膝缓冲了摔倒时的冲击。

e.en: The village {knifesmith} forged blades by hand.
e.zh: 村里的制刀匠用手工锻造刀刃。

e.en: A skilled {knifesmith} can balance a blade perfectly.
e.zh: 熟练的制刀匠能把刀身平衡得恰到好处。

knight-errant.t: 游侠骑士；好管闲事的侠客

e.en: The {knight-errant} rode out to defend the weak.
e.zh: 那位游侠骑士骑马出发去保护弱者。

e.en: He fancied himself a modern {knight-errant}.
e.zh: 他自以为是个现代侠客。

knight-errantry.t: 游侠骑士行为；侠义冒险

e.en: The novel mocks medieval {knight-errantry}.
e.zh: 这部小说嘲弄中世纪的游侠骑士行为。

e.en: His rescue plans had a touch of {knight-errantry}.
e.zh: 他的营救计划带着几分侠义冒险的味道。

e.en: The king granted him {knightage} after the battle.
e.zh: 战后国王授予他骑士身份。

e.en: Old chronicles praised the honor of {knightage}.
e.zh: 古老编年史赞颂骑士阶层的荣誉。

e.en: The poem celebrates true {knighthead} and loyalty.
e.zh: 这首诗歌颂真正的骑士品格与忠诚。

e.en: He won {knighthead} through service, not birth.
e.zh: 他凭服役而非出身获得骑士身份。

e.en: Her courage had a rare {knightliness}.
e.zh: 她的勇气带着罕见的骑士风度。

e.en: The story values mercy as part of {knightliness}.
e.zh: 这个故事把仁慈视为侠义精神的一部分。

e.en: The {knights-errant} searched the forest for danger.
e.zh: 那些游侠骑士在森林里搜寻危险。

e.en: They behaved like {knights-errant} in a comic tale.
e.zh: 他们表现得像滑稽故事里的游侠骑士。

e.en: She bought a potato {knish} from the deli.
e.zh: 她从熟食店买了一个土豆犹太馅饼。

e.en: The warm {knish} smelled of onions and pastry.
e.zh: 热乎乎的犹太馅饼散发着洋葱和面皮的香味。

e.en: The shop sells scarves, sweaters, and other {knitgoods}.
e.zh: 这家店出售围巾、毛衣和其他针织品。

e.en: Winter demand for {knitgoods} rose sharply.
e.zh: 冬季对针织品的需求大幅上升。

e.en: She dropped a {knittingneedle} under the sofa.
e.zh: 她把一根毛线针掉到了沙发下面。

e.en: A wooden {knittingneedle} feels warmer in the hand.
e.zh: 木制编织针握在手里感觉更温润。

e.en: The sailor trimmed the loose {knittles} from the rope.
e.zh: 水手剪掉绳子上松散的小绳结。

e.en: Old netting was covered with {knittles} and frayed ends.
e.zh: 旧网布上满是小绳结和磨散的线头。

e.en: Her {knitwork} showed careful patterns and colors.
e.zh: 她的针织物呈现出精心设计的花纹和颜色。

e.en: He learned {knitwork} during the long winter evenings.
e.zh: 他在漫长的冬夜里学会了针织活。

e.en: The {knobbiness} of the root made it hard to peel.
e.zh: 这根块茎疙疙瘩瘩，很难削皮。

e.en: She liked the {knobbiness} of the old walking stick.
e.zh: 她喜欢那根旧手杖凹凸不平的质感。

e.en: A small {knobble} stuck out from the branch.
e.zh: 树枝上突出来一个小圆疙瘩。

e.en: The disease can {knobble} the surface of the fruit.
e.zh: 这种病会使水果表面长出疙瘩。

e.en: He held a {knobbled} stick in one hand.
e.zh: 他一只手握着一根多节疙瘩的手杖。

e.en: The {knobbled} potatoes were ugly but delicious.
e.zh: 那些凹凸不平的土豆样子难看却很好吃。

e.en: The craftsman tapped the leather with a {knobbler}.
e.zh: 工匠用小圆木槌轻敲皮革。

e.en: A hard {knobbler} formed on the damaged branch.
e.zh: 受损的树枝上形成了一个坚硬的疙瘩状物。

e.en: Weathering was {knobbling} the surface of the stone.
e.zh: 风化正在让石头表面变得疙疙瘩瘩。

e.en: The {knobbling} on the bark showed old injuries.
e.zh: 树皮上的结节显示出旧伤痕。

e.en: The {knobcone} pine grows in dry coastal hills.
e.zh: 瘤果松生长在干燥的海岸丘陵地带。

e.en: Fire can help a {knobcone} release its seeds.
e.zh: 火能帮助瘤果松释放种子。

e.en: The brass {knobhead} was polished smooth.
e.zh: 黄铜旋钮头被擦得很光滑。

e.en: He called the careless driver a {knobhead}.
e.zh: 他骂那个粗心司机是个笨蛋。

e.en: The guard carried a carved {knobkerrie}.
e.zh: 守卫拿着一根雕刻过的南非圆头短棍。

e.en: A {knobkerrie} can serve as both tool and weapon.
e.zh: 南非圆头短棍既可作工具，也可作武器。

e.en: The farmer leaned on a heavy {knobstick}.
e.zh: 农夫倚着一根沉重的圆头棍。

e.en: His old {knobstick} was polished by years of use.
e.zh: 他的旧多节手杖因多年使用而被磨得发亮。

e.en: Losing the contract was a serious {knock-back}.
e.zh: 失去那份合同是一次严重挫折。

e.en: Her proposal received a polite {knock-back}.
e.zh: 她的提议遭到了礼貌的拒绝。

e.en: The boxer scored a {knock-down} in the second round.
e.zh: 拳击手在第二回合把对手击倒了一次。

e.en: They sold the chairs at {knock-down} prices.
e.zh: 他们以大幅降价的价格出售这些椅子。

knock-down-and-drag-out.t: 激烈混战的；毫不留情的

e.en: The debate became a {knock-down-and-drag-out} fight.
e.zh: 那场辩论变成了一场毫不留情的激烈争斗。

e.en: They had a {knock-down-and-drag-out} argument over money.
e.zh: 他们为钱大吵了一场，场面非常激烈。

knock-down-drag-out.t: 激烈混战的；毫不留情的

e.en: It was a {knock-down-drag-out} battle from the start.
e.zh: 那从一开始就是一场激烈混战。

e.en: The siblings had a {knock-down-drag-out} quarrel upstairs.
e.zh: 兄弟姐妹们在楼上大吵了一架，毫不留情。

e.en: Tiny {knubs} of rock stuck out from the wall.
e.zh: 墙上突出了许多小小的岩石疙瘩。

e.en: The old sweater was covered with woolly {knubs}.
e.zh: 那件旧毛衣上满是毛茸茸的小结。

e.en: The doctor pointed to the {knuckle-bone} on the X-ray.
e.zh: 医生指着X光片上的指关节骨。

e.en: Children once played games with a polished {knuckle-bone}.
e.zh: 过去孩子们会用磨光的距骨玩游戏。

e.en: Police found a {knuckle-duster} in his coat pocket.
e.zh: 警方在他的外套口袋里发现了一个指节铜套。

e.en: The museum displayed an old brass {knuckle-duster}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一只旧的黄铜铁拳套。

e.en: He was arrested for carrying {knuckle-dusters}.
e.zh: 他因携带指节铜套而被逮捕。

e.en: The antique shop refused to sell old {knuckle-dusters}.
e.zh: 那家古董店拒绝出售旧铁拳套。

e.en: She bruised a {knucklebone} during the fight.
e.zh: 她在打斗中碰伤了一块指关节骨。

e.en: The archaeologist found a carved {knucklebone} near the hearth.
e.zh: 考古学家在炉边发现了一枚雕刻过的距骨游戏子。

e.en: The carpenter cut around a dark {knur} in the plank.
e.zh: 木匠绕开木板上一处深色的硬木节切割。

e.en: A rough {knur} under the bark caught his knife.
e.zh: 树皮下一个粗硬的小节卡住了他的刀。

e.en: The metal handle has a rough {knurl} for grip.
e.zh: 金属手柄上有粗糙的滚花纹，便于抓握。

e.en: He noticed a dark {knurl} in the old oak board.
e.zh: 他注意到那块旧橡木板里有一个深色硬木节。

e.en: The tool's {knurling} kept it from slipping.
e.zh: 工具上的滚花纹让它不容易打滑。

e.en: The machinist finished the {knurling} on the steel knob.
e.zh: 机工完成了钢旋钮上的滚花加工。

e.en: A {knurly} branch scraped against the window.
e.zh: 一根多节的树枝刮到了窗户。

e.en: His hands were {knurly} from years of hard work.
e.zh: 多年辛苦劳作让他的双手变得粗糙扭结。

e.en: The boy struck the {knurr} across the field.
e.zh: 男孩把木节球击向田野另一边。

e.en: A hard {knurr} made the timber difficult to plane.
e.zh: 一个坚硬的木节让这块木料很难刨平。

e.en: The {knurry} log dulled the saw quickly.
e.zh: 那根多木节的原木很快把锯子磨钝了。

e.en: He chose a {knurry} stick for its strange shape.
e.zh: 他挑了一根粗硬结节的棍子，因为形状很特别。

e.en: The guitar was made from polished {koa}.
e.zh: 这把吉他是用抛光的夏威夷相思木制成的。

e.en: A tall {koa} shaded the trail in the valley.
e.zh: 一棵高大的夏威夷相思树给山谷小路遮阴。

e.en: A male {kob} stood near the marsh.
e.zh: 一只雄性非洲水羚站在沼泽旁。

e.en: The guide spotted a herd of {kob} at dawn.
e.zh: 向导在黎明时发现了一群非洲水羚。

e.en: The old shield was covered with tough {koba}.
e.zh: 那面旧盾牌覆着坚韧的非洲野牛皮革。

e.en: Traders valued {koba} for its strength and thickness.
e.zh: 商人看重非洲野牛皮革的结实和厚度。

e.en: She asked for directions at the nearest {koban}.
e.zh: 她在最近的日本小型派出所问路。

e.en: A friendly officer stepped out of the {koban}.
e.zh: 一位友好的警员从小派出所里走了出来。

e.en: The mineral sample contained rare {kobeite}.
e.zh: 这份矿物样本中含有稀有的铈钛铌矿。

e.en: Geologists identified {kobeite} under the microscope.
e.zh: 地质学家在显微镜下鉴定出了铈钛铌矿。

e.en: The doctor checked whether her {kneepan} had shifted after the fall.
e.zh: 医生检查她摔倒后膝盖骨是否移位。

e.en: An old anatomy book called the patella the {kneepan}.
e.zh: 一本旧解剖书把髌骨称作kneepan。

e.en: The armor's {kneepiece} was dented in the tournament.
e.zh: 那副盔甲的护膝片在比赛中被撞凹了。

e.en: She replaced the worn {kneepiece} on the prosthetic brace.
e.zh: 她更换了假肢支架上磨损的膝部零件。

kneeroom.t: 膝部空间；腿部活动余地

e.en: This small car has very little {kneeroom} in the back.
e.zh: 这辆小车后排的膝部空间很小。

e.en: He chose an aisle seat for extra {kneeroom}.
e.zh: 他选了靠过道的座位，好多一点腿部活动余地。

e.en: They had a proper {knees-up} after the wedding.
e.zh: 婚礼后他们办了一场热闹的欢庆派对。

e.en: The pub hosted a Christmas {knees-up} for the village.
e.zh: 酒吧为村里人办了一场圣诞热闹聚会。

e.en: The club was famous for its noisy {knees-ups}.
e.zh: 这家俱乐部以吵闹热烈的聚会出名。

e.en: Family {knees-ups} filled the house every summer.
e.zh: 每年夏天，家庭欢聚都会让屋子热闹起来。

kneesie.t: 亲昵碰膝；膝部亲昵动作

e.en: They played {kneesie} under the restaurant table.
e.zh: 他们在餐桌下亲昵地用膝盖碰来碰去。

e.en: The old novel described a flirtatious game of {kneesie}.
e.zh: 那本旧小说描写了一场带调情意味的碰膝游戏。

kneesy.t: 膝部突出的；爱用膝碰人的

e.en: The portrait showed a thin, {kneesy} child in shorts.
e.zh: 画像里是个穿短裤、膝盖突出的瘦孩子。

e.en: He became awkward and {kneesy} on the crowded bench.
e.zh: 他坐在拥挤的长凳上，膝盖总碰到别人，显得很别扭。

e.en: A tiny {knib} of metal caught on the cloth.
e.zh: 一个小小的金属尖突钩住了布料。

e.en: The carpenter shaved the rough {knib} from the peg.
e.zh: 木匠把木栓上粗糙的小突起削掉了。

e.en: There was a small {knick} on the edge of the table.
e.zh: 桌子边缘有一道小刻痕。

e.en: He noticed a {knick} in the knife before using it.
e.zh: 他使用前注意到刀口上有个小缺口。

e.en: Every shelf held a dusty {knick-knack} from her travels.
e.zh: 每个架子上都有她旅行带回来的落灰小摆设。

e.en: He bought a cheap {knick-knack} at the market.
e.zh: 他在市场买了个便宜的小装饰品。

e.en: A porcelain {knickknack} sat beside the lamp.
e.zh: 灯旁放着一个瓷制小摆设。

e.en: She dislikes clutter, so every {knickknack} must earn its place.
e.zh: 她不喜欢杂乱，所以每个小装饰品都得有留下的理由。

knickknackery.t: 小摆设集合；廉价装饰品

e.en: The mantelpiece was crowded with Victorian {knickknackery}.
e.zh: 壁炉架上挤满了维多利亚风格的小摆设。

e.en: He dismissed the souvenirs as tourist {knickknackery}.
e.zh: 他把那些纪念品看成游客爱买的廉价装饰品。

knickpoint.t: 河流坡折点；地貌转折点

e.en: The waterfall marks a clear {knickpoint} in the river profile.
e.zh: 这处瀑布标志着河流纵剖面上的明显坡折点。

e.en: Erosion slowly moved the {knickpoint} upstream.
e.zh: 侵蚀作用慢慢把这个地貌转折点向上游推进。

e.en: He wore old wool {knicks} for the costume party.
e.zh: 他穿着旧羊毛灯笼裤去参加化装派对。

e.en: The golfer's {knicks} looked comically formal today.
e.zh: 那位高尔夫球手今天的短裤显得滑稽地正式。

e.en: The {knife-blade} flashed in the kitchen light.
e.zh: 刀刃在厨房灯光下闪了一下。

e.en: A thin {knife-blade} can slice tomatoes cleanly.
e.zh: 薄薄的刀身能把番茄切得很利落。

e.en: The servant polished the cutlery on a {knife-board}.
e.zh: 仆人在擦刀板上擦亮餐具。

e.en: An antique {knife-board} hung beside the old stove.
e.zh: 一块古旧的磨刀板挂在老炉子旁边。

e.en: The climber balanced on a narrow {knife-edge} ridge.
e.zh: 登山者在狭窄如刀刃的山脊上保持平衡。

e.en: The election remained on a {knife-edge} until midnight.
e.zh: 选举结果直到午夜仍处在胜负难分的危险边缘。

e.en: A {knife-edged} ridge separated the two valleys.
e.zh: 一道刀刃般险峻的山脊隔开了两条山谷。

e.en: Her {knife-edged} reply silenced the room.
e.zh: 她锋利如刀的回答让全场安静下来。

e.en: The machine tests tiny loads on polished {knife-edges}.
e.zh: 这台机器在抛光刀刃支点上测试微小载荷。

e.en: Several races were balanced on political {knife-edges}.
e.zh: 几场竞选都处在政治上胜负难料的边缘。

e.en: She found a wooden {knifeboard} in the pantry.
e.zh: 她在食品储藏室里找到一块木制擦刀板。

e.en: The old {knifeboard} still smelled faintly of polish.
e.zh: 那块旧磨刀板仍隐约有抛光剂的气味。

e.en: The scale rested on a delicate {knifeedge}.
e.zh: 天平架在一个精细的刀刃支点上。

e.en: Their finances were on a {knifeedge} after the layoffs.
e.zh: 裁员后，他们的财务状况处在危险边缘。

e.en: The aquarium kept a silver {knifefish} in a dim tank.
e.zh: 水族馆把一条银色刀鱼养在昏暗的鱼缸里。

e.en: A {knifefish} moves with a rippling fin along its belly.
e.zh: 刀形鱼靠腹部波动的鳍游动。

e.en: A {knifelike} pain shot through his shoulder.
e.zh: 一阵刀割般的疼痛穿过他的肩膀。

e.en: The mountain had a {knifelike} ridge of black rock.
e.zh: 那座山有一道像刀刃般的黑色岩脊。

e.en: Place the carving knife on the silver {kniferest}.
e.zh: 把切肉刀放在银制刀架上。

e.en: Each formal place setting included a glass {kniferest}.
e.zh: 每套餐桌正式摆设里都有一个玻璃餐刀托。

e.en: The doctor said the child's {knock-knee} might improve naturally.
e.zh: 医生说这个孩子的膝外翻可能会自然好转。

e.en: Severe {knock-knee} can make walking uncomfortable.
e.zh: 严重的X形腿会让走路变得不舒服。

e.en: The {knock-kneed} boy avoided running in gym class.
e.zh: 那个X形腿的男孩在体育课上不愿跑步。

e.en: She stood awkwardly, slightly {knock-kneed} and nervous.
e.zh: 她有些膝外翻，紧张地别扭站着。

e.en: Many toddlers grow out of {knock-knees} by school age.
e.zh: 许多幼儿到上学年龄时X形腿会自行改善。

e.en: His {knock-knees} caused pain during long walks.
e.zh: 他的膝外翻让他走远路时感到疼痛。

e.en: She bought a cheap {knock-off} handbag at the market.
e.zh: 她在市场买了一个便宜的仿冒手提包。

e.en: We usually {knock-off} work around six.
e.zh: 我们通常六点左右下班。

e.en: The strike had a {knock-on} effect on deliveries.
e.zh: 罢工对送货产生了连带影响。

e.en: Higher fuel prices created {knock-on} costs for shoppers.
e.zh: 燃油涨价给购物者带来了后续成本。

knock-out.t: 淘汰赛；击倒；极出色的人

e.en: The final was a tense {knock-out} match.
e.zh: 决赛是一场紧张的淘汰赛。

e.en: Her black dress was a real {knock-out}.
e.zh: 她那条黑裙子真是惊艳极了。

e.en: He joked crudely that his friend had {knocked-up} his girlfriend.
e.zh: 他粗俗地开玩笑说朋友让女友怀孕了。

e.en: I can {knock-up} a quick meal in ten minutes.
e.zh: 我能在十分钟内匆忙做出一顿便饭。

e.en: Engineers tested the fuel's {knockability} under high pressure.
e.zh: 工程师在高压下测试这种燃料的耐爆震性。

e.en: The material's {knockability} mattered for the instrument design.
e.zh: 这种材料的可敲击性对乐器设计很重要。

e.en: Losing the contract was a serious {knockback} for the company.
e.zh: 失去合同对公司来说是一次严重挫折。

e.en: The rifle's {knockback} surprised the new shooter.
e.zh: 步枪的后坐力让新手射手吃了一惊。

knockdown-dragout.t: 激烈混战的；拼死争斗的

e.en: They had a {knockdown-dragout} argument about the inheritance.
e.zh: 他们为遗产问题大吵了一场，争得非常激烈。

e.en: The teams played a {knockdown-dragout} final in heavy rain.
e.zh: 两队在大雨中打了一场拼到最后的决赛。

e.en: The {knocked-down} boxer slowly got back up.
e.zh: 被击倒的拳击手慢慢站了起来。

e.en: The table arrived {knocked-down} in a flat box.
e.zh: 桌子以拆散包装的形式装在扁盒里送到。

e.en: The fighter was {knocked-out} in the second round.
e.zh: 那名拳手在第二回合被击昏了。

e.en: Our team was {knocked-out} before the semifinals.
e.zh: 我们队在半决赛前就被淘汰了。

e.en: The old cartoon showed a {knockkneed} clerk carrying boxes.
e.zh: 那幅老漫画画着一个X形腿的职员搬箱子。

e.en: He felt self-conscious about his {knockkneed} stance.
e.zh: 他对自己膝外翻的站姿感到不自在。

knockon.t: 连带影响；橄榄球前传球失误

e.en: The delay caused a serious {knockon} across the schedule.
e.zh: 这次延误对整个日程造成了严重连带影响。

e.en: The referee called a {knockon} after the ball slipped forward.
e.zh: 球向前滑落后，裁判判了前传球失误。

e.en: The slang verb {knockup} can sound offensive.
e.zh: 俚语动词knockup听起来可能很冒犯。

e.en: They could {knockup} a shelter before dark.
e.zh: 他们能在天黑前匆忙搭出一个避难处。

e.en: He grilled {knockwurst} for the picnic lunch.
e.zh: 他为野餐午餐烤了德国蒜味熏香肠。

e.en: The deli served {knockwurst} with mustard and sauerkraut.
e.zh: 熟食店供应配芥末和酸菜的德国蒜味熏香肠。

e.en: A small {knop} rose from the carved wooden handle.
e.zh: 雕花木柄上凸起了一个小圆疙瘩。

e.en: The hillside ended in a grassy {knop}.
e.zh: 山坡尽头是一处长满草的小圆丘。

e.en: The mineral sample was identified as {knopite}.
e.zh: 这块矿物样本被鉴定为硫酸铝钾矿物。

e.en: Few collectors had ever seen {knopite} in person.
e.zh: 很少有收藏者亲眼见过knopite这种矿物。

e.en: The museum displayed a carved {knopkierie} from southern Africa.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一根来自南部非洲的雕花圆头木棒。

e.en: He carried a {knopkierie} during the traditional dance.
e.zh: 他在传统舞蹈中拿着一根南非圆头木棒。

e.en: The chair had {knopped} legs and a polished seat.
e.zh: 这把椅子的腿有圆突装饰，座面也打磨得很亮。

e.en: She chose a {knopped} walking stick from the rack.
e.zh: 她从架子上选了一根带节结的手杖。

e.en: A squirrel peered through the {knot-hole} in the fence.
e.zh: 一只松鼠从栅栏上的节孔里探头看。

e.en: The old board had a dark {knot-hole} near the edge.
e.zh: 那块旧木板靠边有一个发黑的树节孔。

e.en: The path was partly covered with {knotgrass}.
e.zh: 小路有一部分被蓼类杂草覆盖。

e.en: Farmers pulled {knotgrass} from the vegetable beds.
e.zh: 农民把菜畦里的萹蓄拔掉。

e.en: Only a {knothead} would park there.
e.zh: 只有笨蛋才会把车停在那里。

e.en: Stop acting like a {knothead} and listen.
e.zh: 别再像个傻瓜一样，听我说。

e.en: She bought a {knotless} fishing net.
e.zh: 她买了一张无结渔网。

e.en: The carpenter chose {knotless} pine for the cabinet doors.
e.zh: 木匠选用没有节疤的松木来做柜门。

e.en: The vines grew {knottily} around the gate.
e.zh: 藤蔓纠结地缠绕在大门周围。

e.en: The argument was {knottily} phrased and hard to follow.
e.zh: 这段论证写得复杂难解，很难跟上。

e.en: The {knottiness} of the oak made carving difficult.
e.zh: 橡木节疤太多，使雕刻变得困难。

e.en: She underestimated the {knottiness} of the dispute.
e.zh: 她低估了这场争议的复杂棘手程度。

e.en: Japanese {knotweed} damaged the garden wall.
e.zh: 日本虎杖损坏了花园的围墙。

e.en: The council hired workers to remove {knotweed}.
e.zh: 市政会雇人清除蓼属杂草。

e.en: The manuscript border was filled with Celtic {knotwork}.
e.zh: 手稿边框布满了凯尔特绳结纹饰。

e.en: She studied the {knotwork} carved into the stone cross.
e.zh: 她端详着刻在石十字架上的结形装饰。

e.en: The prisoner feared the {knout} more than the cell.
e.zh: 囚犯害怕那条俄式皮鞭，甚于牢房本身。

e.en: The tyrant ordered soldiers to {knout} the rebels.
e.zh: 暴君命令士兵用皮鞭抽打叛乱者。

e.en: The old law allowed {knouting} as punishment.
e.zh: 那条旧法律允许以鞭刑作为惩罚。

e.en: They protested the {knouting} of political prisoners.
e.zh: 他们抗议对政治犯实施皮鞭抽打。

e.en: The guards carried heavy {knouts}.
e.zh: 卫兵们带着沉重的俄式皮鞭。

e.en: History records how the regime {knouts} dissenters.
e.zh: 历史记载了该政权如何用皮鞭抽打异见者。

e.en: Nobody enjoys working with a {know-all}.
e.zh: 没人喜欢和自以为什么都懂的人共事。

e.en: He sounded like a {know-all} during the meeting.
e.zh: 他在会上听起来像个自以为无所不知的人。

e.en: The class had two noisy {know-alls}.
e.zh: 班里有两个吵闹的自以为是者。

e.en: Managers should not reward {know-alls} who ignore advice.
e.zh: 管理者不该奖励那些无视建议的万事通式人物。

e.en: Don't be such a {know-it-all}.
e.zh: 别这么自以为什么都懂。

e.en: The new intern sounded like a {know-it-all} at first.
e.zh: 那个新实习生一开始听起来像个万事通。

e.en: Online forums attract plenty of {know-it-alls}.
e.zh: 网络论坛吸引了很多自以为什么都懂的人。

e.en: She avoids meetings full of {know-it-alls}.
e.zh: 她避开那些全是万事通的会议。

e.en: He dismissed the critic as a {know-nothing}.
e.zh: 他把那位批评者贬为无知之辈。

e.en: The article attacked {know-nothing} politics.
e.zh: 这篇文章抨击了反智式政治。

know-nothingism.t: 无知主义；反智排外主义

e.en: The speech warned against rising {know-nothingism}.
e.zh: 这场演讲警告人们警惕日益抬头的无知主义。

e.en: Historians link {know-nothingism} with nativist politics.
e.zh: 历史学家把反智排外主义与本土主义政治联系起来。

knowability.t: 可知性；能被认识的性质

e.en: Philosophers debate the {knowability} of the external world.
e.zh: 哲学家争论外部世界的可知性。

e.en: The experiment improved the {knowability} of the system's behavior.
e.zh: 这项实验提高了该系统行为的可认识程度。

e.en: Thou {knowest} the truth already.
e.zh: 你其实早已知道真相。

e.en: Lord, thou {knowest} my weakness.
e.zh: 主啊，你知道我的软弱。

e.en: Use your {knowledge-box} before answering.
e.zh: 回答之前先动动你的脑子。

e.en: The app became a shared {knowledge-box} for the team.
e.zh: 这个应用成了团队共享的知识盒子。

e.en: Software design is a {knowledge-intensive} activity.
e.zh: 软件设计是一项知识密集型活动。

e.en: The region attracts {knowledge-intensive} industries.
e.zh: 该地区吸引了知识密集型产业。

e.en: Her {knowledgeability} impressed the interview panel.
e.zh: 她的博学给面试小组留下了深刻印象。

e.en: Customers valued his {knowledgeability} about rare wines.
e.zh: 顾客看重他对稀有葡萄酒的丰富知识。

knowledgeble.t: 拼写错误，意为知识渊博的

e.en: The review called him {knowledgeble}, though the word was misspelled.
e.zh: 那篇评论把他说成知识渊博，但这个词拼错了。

e.en: She typed {knowledgeble} instead of knowledgeable in the report.
e.zh: 她在报告里把 knowledgeable 误打成了 knowledgeble。

e.en: The miner blamed a {kobold} for the strange noises underground.
e.zh: 矿工把地下奇怪的声音归咎于一个小妖精。

e.en: In the old tale, a {kobold} guarded the hidden treasure.
e.zh: 在那个古老故事里，一个小妖精守着隐藏的宝藏。

e.en: A {koedoe} stood quietly near the edge of the trees.
e.zh: 一只捻角羚静静地站在树林边。

e.en: The hunter recognized the spiral horns of the {koedoe}.
e.zh: 猎人认出了那只大羚羊的螺旋形角。

e.en: A {koel} called loudly before sunrise.
e.zh: 日出前，一只噪鹃大声鸣叫。

e.en: She heard the {koel} in the mango tree.
e.zh: 她听见芒果树上有一只噪鹃在叫。

e.en: Several {koels} called from the garden at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时，几只噪鹃在花园里鸣叫。

e.en: The children watched two {koels} fly over the roof.
e.zh: 孩子们看见两只噪鹃飞过屋顶。

e.en: The sample contained tiny crystals of {koenlite}.
e.zh: 这个样品含有细小的科恩石晶体。

e.en: Collectors value {koenlite} because it is rarely found.
e.zh: 收藏者看重科恩石，因为它很少被发现。

e.en: The pale pink crust was identified as {koettigite}.
e.zh: 那层淡粉色外壳被鉴定为钴砷华。

e.en: Miners found {koettigite} in the old cobalt deposit.
e.zh: 矿工在旧钴矿床中发现了钴砷华。

e.en: She served lamb {kofta} with yogurt sauce.
e.zh: 她端上了配酸奶酱的羊肉香料肉丸。

e.en: The vegetarian {kofta} was made with potatoes and peas.
e.zh: 那道素香料丸子是用土豆和豌豆做的。

e.en: Iron deficiency can cause {koilonychia} in severe cases.
e.zh: 严重缺铁时可能会引起匙状指甲症。

e.en: The doctor noticed {koilonychia} during the hand examination.
e.zh: 医生在检查手部时注意到匙状指甲症。

e.en: Greek {koine} spread across the eastern Mediterranean.
e.zh: 希腊共同语曾在东地中海地区传播。

e.en: The traders developed a local {koine} for everyday business.
e.zh: 商人们形成了一种本地通用语来处理日常生意。

e.en: The brewer added {koji} to start the fermentation.
e.zh: 酿造师加入米曲来启动发酵。

e.en: Miso gets much of its flavor from {koji}.
e.zh: 味噌的许多风味都来自米曲。

e.en: The lab measured {kojibiose} in the fermented sample.
e.zh: 实验室测定了发酵样品中的曲二糖。

e.en: {Kojibiose} is a disaccharide found in some starch products.
e.zh: 曲二糖是一种存在于某些淀粉制品中的二糖。

e.en: Researchers grew {kok-saghyz} as a source of natural rubber.
e.zh: 研究人员种植橡胶蒲公英作为天然橡胶来源。

e.en: The roots of {kok-saghyz} contain usable latex.
e.zh: 橡胶蒲公英的根部含有可利用的乳胶。

e.en: Farmers tested {kok-sagyz} in a small rubber crop trial.
e.zh: 农民在一项小型橡胶作物试验中种植了橡胶蒲公英。

e.en: {Kok-sagyz} attracted interest during rubber shortages.
e.zh: 在橡胶短缺时期，橡胶蒲公英引起了人们的兴趣。

e.en: She bought a painted {kokeshi} at the craft shop.
e.zh: 她在手工艺品店买了一个彩绘日本木偶娃娃。

e.en: Traditional {kokeshi} have simple bodies and round heads.
e.zh: 传统日本木偶娃娃有简洁的身体和圆圆的头。

e.en: The estate produced several thousand {koku} of rice.
e.zh: 这片领地产出了数千石大米。

e.en: A samurai's income was often counted in {koku}.
e.zh: 武士的收入常按石这个单位来计算。

e.en: The chemist isolated {kokusaginine} from the plant extract.
e.zh: 化学家从植物提取物中分离出臭茱萸碱。

e.en: Studies examined whether {kokusaginine} affects cell growth.
e.zh: 研究考察了臭茱萸碱是否会影响细胞生长。

e.en: Grandma baked apricot {kolacky} for the holiday.
e.zh: 奶奶为节日烤了杏子果酱小甜饼。

e.en: The bakery sells {kolacky} filled with cheese or jam.
e.zh: 这家面包店卖夹奶酪或果酱的 kolacky 小甜饼。

e.en: The paper described {kolanin} in kola nut extracts.
e.zh: 论文描述了可乐果提取物中的可乐果苷。

e.en: Analysts compared {kolanin} levels in several samples.
e.zh: 分析人员比较了几个样品中的可乐果苷含量。

e.en: Early pharmacology texts mention {kolatin} from kola seeds.
e.zh: 早期药理学文献提到来自可乐果种子的可乐果苦素。

e.en: The extract's bitterness was partly attributed to {kolatin}.
e.zh: 这种提取物的苦味部分归因于可乐果苦素。

e.en: The collector labeled the green crystals as {kolbeckite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把这些绿色晶体标注为水磷铝锶石。

e.en: {Kolbeckite} can occur in phosphate-rich mineral deposits.
e.zh: 水磷铝锶石可能出现在富含磷酸盐的矿床中。

e.en: They went outside to smoke some {koosh}.
e.zh: 他们到外面去抽点大麻。

e.en: The room smelled strongly of {koosh}.
e.zh: 房间里有很重的大麻味。

e.en: A narrow {kope} rose above the old roof.
e.zh: 一座狭窄的小塔耸立在旧屋顶上。

e.en: The guard watched the road from the {kope}.
e.zh: 守卫从塔楼上观察道路。

e.en: He paid the fare with a single {kopek}.
e.zh: 他用一枚戈比付了车费。

e.en: The old coin was worth less than a {kopek}.
e.zh: 那枚旧币的价值还不到一个戈比。

e.en: The letter {koph} appears in the old inscription.
e.zh: 字母科夫出现在那段古老铭文中。

e.en: She practiced writing {koph} in Hebrew class.
e.zh: 她在希伯来语课上练习书写科夫这个字母。

e.en: His {kopophobia} made him avoid any strenuous exercise.
e.zh: 他对疲劳的恐惧使他避免任何剧烈运动。

e.en: The therapist discussed {kopophobia} with the anxious patient.
e.zh: 治疗师和那位焦虑的病人讨论了对疲劳的恐惧。

e.en: The soldier tightened his {koppel} before inspection.
e.zh: 士兵在检阅前收紧了军用皮带。

e.en: An old leather {koppel} hung beside the uniform.
e.zh: 一条旧皮腰带挂在制服旁边。

e.en: We climbed the {koppie} to watch the sunset.
e.zh: 我们爬上小山丘看日落。

e.en: A few trees grew on the rocky {koppie}.
e.zh: 岩石小丘上长着几棵树。

e.en: The cattle grazed between the {koppies}.
e.zh: 牛群在几座小山丘之间吃草。

e.en: Low {koppies} broke the flat horizon.
e.zh: 低矮的小圆丘打破了平坦的地平线。

e.en: They drove a battered {kombi} along the coast.
e.zh: 他们开着一辆破旧的小型客货两用车沿海岸行驶。

e.en: The hostel sent a {kombi} to collect us.
e.zh: 旅舍派了一辆小客货车来接我们。

e.en: She drinks {kombucha} instead of soda.
e.zh: 她喝康普茶来代替汽水。

e.en: The cafe sells ginger {kombucha} in glass bottles.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆出售玻璃瓶装的姜味康普茶。

e.en: The villagers reported to the {kommandatura} each morning.
e.zh: 村民们每天早上都要向军事司令部报到。

e.en: A notice from the {kommandatura} closed the market.
e.zh: 占领当局的一纸通知关闭了市场。

e.en: A white {komondor} guarded the farm gate.
e.zh: 一只白色可蒙犬守在农场门口。

e.en: The {komondor}'s corded coat needs careful care.
e.zh: 可蒙犬绳状的毛发需要细心打理。

e.en: He joined the {Komsomol} as a teenager.
e.zh: 他十几岁时加入了苏联共青团。

e.en: The novel describes a local {Komsomol} meeting.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了一次地方共青团会议。

e.en: The old {konak} overlooks the river.
e.zh: 那座古老的奥斯曼式大宅俯瞰着河流。

e.en: Officials met inside the restored {konak}.
e.zh: 官员们在修复后的官邸里会面。

e.en: The painter cleaned her {kolinskies} after finishing the watercolor study.
e.zh: 画家完成水彩习作后清洗了她的西伯利亚鼬毛画笔。

e.en: Fine {kolinskies} are prized for their sharp points and spring.
e.zh: 优质西伯利亚鼬毛画笔因笔尖锐利、弹性好而受重视。

kolinsky.t: 西伯利亚鼬毛；鼬毛画笔

e.en: She bought a {kolinsky} brush for detailed watercolor work.
e.zh: 她买了一支西伯利亚鼬毛画笔来画细致的水彩。

e.en: The coat was trimmed with rare {kolinsky} fur.
e.zh: 那件外套镶了稀有的西伯利亚鼬毛皮。

e.en: The novel follows a young {kolkhoznik} during the harvest season.
e.zh: 这部小说写一名年轻集体农庄庄员在收获季节的经历。

e.en: As a former {kolkhoznik}, he remembered the strict quotas clearly.
e.zh: 作为曾经的集体农庄庄员，他清楚记得那些严格定额。

e.en: Her first {kollagraph} used sandpaper, string, and torn cardboard.
e.zh: 她的第一幅拼贴版画用了砂纸、细绳和撕开的纸板。

e.en: The class printed a {kollagraph} from a textured plate.
e.zh: 全班用有纹理的拼贴印版印出了一幅版画。

e.en: The old factory used a {kollergang} to crush clay.
e.zh: 那家老工厂用轮碾机压碎黏土。

e.en: A restored {kollergang} stood beside the museum kiln.
e.zh: 一台修复好的轮碾机放在博物馆窑炉旁。

e.en: The guests joined a lively {kolo} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后，客人们加入了一场热闹的科洛环舞。

e.en: A slow {kolo} opened the village festival.
e.zh: 村庄节庆以一支缓慢的科洛民间舞开场。

e.en: The violinist rubbed {kolophonium} on the bow before rehearsal.
e.zh: 小提琴手排练前在琴弓上擦了松香。

e.en: A small cake of {kolophonium} lay in the instrument case.
e.zh: 乐器盒里放着一小块松香。

e.en: The chemist described the process as {kolytic} rather than purely mechanical.
e.zh: 化学家把这个过程描述为胶质分解的，而不是单纯机械作用。

e.en: A {kolytic} reaction weakened the gel structure overnight.
e.zh: 一种胶质分解反应在一夜之间削弱了凝胶结构。

e.en: The singer softened the phrase with a {komal} note.
e.zh: 歌手用一个印度音乐中的降音让乐句变得柔和。

e.en: In this raga, the {komal} form changes the mood completely.
e.zh: 在这首拉格中，降音形式完全改变了情绪。

e.en: The museum displayed a marble {kore} near the entrance.
e.zh: 博物馆在入口附近展出了一尊大理石古希腊少女雕像。

e.en: A painted {kore} once stood as a temple offering.
e.zh: 一尊上过彩的少女雕像曾作为神庙供奉品立在那里。

e.en: The path was lined with flowering {koromiko}.
e.zh: 小路两旁长满了开花的科罗米科灌木。

e.en: Some herbal remedies use dried {koromiko} leaves.
e.zh: 一些草药疗法会使用晒干的科罗米科叶。

e.en: The souvenir cost one hundred Czech {koruna}.
e.zh: 这件纪念品花了一百捷克克朗。

e.en: Prices were still listed in {koruna} on the old menu.
e.zh: 旧菜单上的价格仍然用克朗标示。

e.en: She exchanged fifty dollars for Czech {korunas}.
e.zh: 她把五十美元换成了捷克克朗。

e.en: The bill came to eight hundred {korunas}.
e.zh: 账单总共是八百克朗。

e.en: The ticket price was shown as three hundred {koruny}.
e.zh: 票价标为三百克朗。

e.en: He had only a few {koruny} left after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后他只剩下几枚克朗了。

e.en: The archive includes recordings of {Koryak} songs.
e.zh: 档案中收有科里亚克语歌曲的录音。

e.en: A {Koryak} elder described life on the tundra.
e.zh: 一位科里亚克族长者讲述了苔原上的生活。

e.en: The old remedy contained powdered {koso}.
e.zh: 这种旧药方里含有磨成粉的苦苏花。

e.en: Traders once sold {koso} as an anthelmintic herb.
e.zh: 商人过去曾把苦苏花当作驱虫草药出售。

e.en: A {konik} grazed quietly near the marsh.
e.zh: 一匹波兰小型原始马在沼泽旁安静吃草。

e.en: Conservationists use {koniks} to manage wet grasslands.
e.zh: 保护人员用波兰原始马来管理潮湿草地。

e.en: The engineer checked the tunnel air with a {konimeter}.
e.zh: 工程师用空气尘埃测定仪检查隧道空气。

e.en: An old {konimeter} recorded dust levels in the workshop.
e.zh: 一台旧的尘埃测定仪记录了车间里的粉尘水平。

e.en: The lab used a {koniogravimeter} to weigh airborne dust.
e.zh: 实验室用重量式尘埃测定仪称量空气中的粉尘。

e.en: A {koniogravimeter} can collect particles for later analysis.
e.zh: 重量式尘埃测定仪可以收集颗粒以便后续分析。

e.en: Her research in {koniology} focused on factory dust.
e.zh: 她在尘埃学方面的研究集中于工厂粉尘。

e.en: Modern {koniology} helps explain air pollution risks.
e.zh: 现代尘埃学有助于解释空气污染风险。

e.en: Miners once faced a high risk of {koniosis}.
e.zh: 矿工过去曾面临很高的尘肺病风险。

e.en: Doctors diagnosed {koniosis} after years of dust exposure.
e.zh: 多年接触粉尘后，医生诊断出粉尘沉着症。

e.en: The inspector carried a {koniscope} into the mill.
e.zh: 检查员带着空气尘埃计走进磨坊。

e.en: A {koniscope} showed heavy dust in the lecture hall.
e.zh: 空气尘埃计显示讲堂里的灰尘很重。

e.en: Particles settled inside the {konisphere} during the test.
e.zh: 测试期间，颗粒沉积在尘埃采样球室内。

e.en: The technician cleaned the {konisphere} before taking measurements.
e.zh: 技术员在测量前清洁了尘埃采样球室。

e.en: The safety team installed a {konometer} near the furnace.
e.zh: 安全小组在炉子附近安装了空气粉尘测量仪。

e.en: Readings from the {konometer} rose after the drilling began.
e.zh: 钻孔开始后，粉尘测量仪的读数升高了。

e.en: The coil was wound with {konstantan} wire.
e.zh: 这个线圈是用康铜合金线绕成的。

e.en: Engineers chose {konstantan} for its stable resistance.
e.zh: 工程师选择康铜，因为它的电阻较稳定。

e.en: The steel {konzern} controlled mines and factories.
e.zh: 这家钢铁企业集团控制着矿山和工厂。

e.en: A German {konzern} bought the smaller company.
e.zh: 一家德国大型企业集团收购了那家小公司。

e.en: A {koodoo} stood motionless among the trees.
e.zh: 一只捻角羚一动不动地站在树丛中。

e.en: Hunters admired the spiral horns of the {koodoo}.
e.zh: 猎人们欣赏那只大羚羊螺旋状的角。

e.en: Several {koodoos} crossed the dry riverbed.
e.zh: 几只捻角羚穿过干涸的河床。

e.en: The guide pointed out two {koodoos} in the shade.
e.zh: 向导指出阴影里有两只捻角羚。

e.en: A {kookaburra} laughed loudly at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时，一只笑翠鸟大声鸣叫。

e.en: Children watched the {kookaburra} perch on the fence.
e.zh: 孩子们看着笑翠鸟停在篱笆上。

e.en: She wore a {kookie} hat to the party.
e.zh: 她戴着一顶古怪可爱的帽子去参加聚会。

e.en: His {kookie} ideas sometimes worked surprisingly well.
e.zh: 他那些古怪的点子有时竟然很管用。

e.en: The film's {kookiness} made it strangely charming.
e.zh: 这部电影的古怪劲儿让它有种奇特的魅力。

e.en: Her gentle {kookiness} put everyone at ease.
e.zh: 她那种温和的怪趣味让大家都放松下来。

e.en: The travelers were offered {koomis} in a wooden bowl.
e.zh: 旅人们被请喝盛在木碗里的马奶酒。

e.en: Traditional {koomis} is made from fermented mare's milk.
e.zh: 传统马奶酒是用发酵的母马乳制成的。

e.en: A {koorajong} shaded the edge of the paddock.
e.zh: 一棵库拉琼树给牧场边缘投下阴影。

e.en: The old {koorajong} survived many dry summers.
e.zh: 那棵老澳洲瓶树熬过了许多个干旱夏天。

e.en: Many {Kooris} maintain strong ties to their country.
e.zh: 许多澳洲东南部原住民仍与自己的土地保持紧密联系。

e.en: The museum worked with {Kooris} on the exhibition.
e.zh: 博物馆与澳洲东南部原住民合作举办这次展览。

e.en: The old pharmacopoeia listed {kousso} as a remedy for tapeworm.
e.zh: 那本旧药典把苦苏列为治疗绦虫的药物。

e.en: Few modern doctors would prescribe {kousso} today.
e.zh: 如今很少有现代医生会开苦苏这种药。

e.en: The envoy refused to {kow-tow} before the emperor.
e.zh: 那名使节拒绝在皇帝面前叩头。

e.en: She would not {kow-tow} to every demand from her boss.
e.zh: 她不愿对老板的每个要求都卑躬屈膝。

e.en: He {kow-tows} whenever powerful clients enter the room.
e.zh: 每当有权势的客户进屋时，他就卑躬屈膝。

e.en: The ritual record says the visitor {kow-tows} three times.
e.zh: 礼仪记录说来访者要叩头三次。

e.en: A yellow {kowhai} bloomed beside the school gate.
e.zh: 校门旁一棵开黄花的新西兰槐树盛开了。

e.en: Tui birds often feed from {kowhai} flowers in spring.
e.zh: 春天，簇胸吸蜜鸟常在新西兰槐花间取食。

e.en: The clerk would {kowtown} to anyone with money.
e.zh: 那个职员会对任何有钱人卑躬屈膝。

e.en: Pilgrims used to {kowtown} before the shrine.
e.zh: 朝圣者过去会在神龛前叩头。

e.en: The museum displayed a dish of {kraakporselein} from the Ming period.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一只明代克拉克瓷盘。

e.en: Collectors prize {kraakporselein} for its blue-and-white decoration.
e.zh: 收藏家看重克拉克瓷器的青花装饰。

e.en: The parcel was wrapped in brown {kraft-paper}.
e.zh: 包裹用棕色牛皮纸包着。

e.en: Designers chose {kraft-paper} for the rustic menu covers.
e.zh: 设计师选用牛皮纸制作质朴风格的菜单封面。

e.en: Baboons slept safely on the high {krans}.
e.zh: 狒狒安全地睡在高高的南非峭壁上。

e.en: The trail ended below a sheer {krans}.
e.zh: 小径在一道陡直的南非悬崖下方结束。

e.en: The old bill was worth one {krona}.
e.zh: 那张旧钞值一克朗。

e.en: She exchanged dollars for Icelandic {krona}.
e.zh: 她把美元换成了冰岛克朗。

e.en: The coffee cost thirty {kronor}.
e.zh: 这杯咖啡花了三十克朗。

e.en: He saved several hundred Swedish {kronor}.
e.zh: 他攒了几百瑞典克朗。

e.en: The ticket costs two thousand {kronur}.
e.zh: 这张票要两千冰岛克朗。

e.en: She counted the remaining {kronur} carefully.
e.zh: 她仔细数了剩下的冰岛克朗。

e.en: The souvenir cost five {kroon}.
e.zh: 这个纪念品花了五克朗。

e.en: Estonia once used the {kroon}.
e.zh: 爱沙尼亚曾经使用克朗。

e.en: He bought a {krugerrand} as an investment.
e.zh: 他买了一枚南非克鲁格金币作为投资。

e.en: The dealer checked the gold {krugerrand}.
e.zh: 交易商检查了那枚黄金克鲁格金币。

e.en: Collectors traded {krugerrands} at the fair.
e.zh: 收藏者在集市上交易南非克鲁格金币。

e.en: The safe contained several {krugerrands}.
e.zh: 保险箱里有几枚南非克鲁格金币。

e.en: She bought a glazed {kruller} for breakfast.
e.zh: 她买了一个裹糖霜的扭花甜甜圈当早餐。

e.en: The bakery sells fresh {krullers} every morning.
e.zh: 那家面包店每天早上卖新鲜的扭花甜甜圈。

krumhorn.t: 文艺复兴时期弯管簧乐器

e.en: The ensemble featured a soft {krumhorn}.
e.zh: 合奏中有一件声音柔和的弯管簧乐器。

e.en: He repaired an old {krumhorn} for the concert.
e.zh: 他为音乐会修好了一件旧的克鲁姆管。

e.en: The trail passed through dense {krummholz}.
e.zh: 小径穿过一片茂密的高山矮曲林。

e.en: Wind shaped the pines into {krummholz}.
e.zh: 强风把松树塑造成了低矮扭曲的林木。

krummhorn.t: 文艺复兴时期弯管簧乐器

e.en: A {krummhorn} sounded in the Renaissance piece.
e.zh: 那首文艺复兴乐曲里响起了克鲁姆管的声音。

e.en: She learned the {krummhorn} for early music concerts.
e.zh: 她为了早期音乐会学习演奏克鲁姆管。

e.en: The antique dealer showed us a silver {kreutzer}.
e.zh: 古董商给我们看了一枚银质克罗伊策旧币。

e.en: A few {kreutzers} once bought a simple meal.
e.zh: 过去几个克罗伊策就能买一顿简单的饭。

e.en: He found a worn {kreuzer} in the box.
e.zh: 他在盒子里发现了一枚磨损的克罗伊泽旧币。

e.en: The price was listed as three {kreuzers}.
e.zh: 标价写着三个克罗伊泽。

e.en: Her {krewe} designed a float for Mardi Gras.
e.zh: 她所在的狂欢节社团为忏悔星期二设计了一辆彩车。

e.en: The local {krewe} threw beads to the crowd.
e.zh: 当地游行社团向人群抛洒珠链。

e.en: The historian used {krieg} in a German quotation.
e.zh: 历史学家在一段德语引文中用了krieg这个词。

e.en: The team launched a media {krieg} before the vote.
e.zh: 投票前，这个团队发动了一场媒体攻势。

e.en: The officers practiced strategy with {kriegspiel}.
e.zh: 军官们用军事推演棋练习战略。

e.en: In {kriegspiel}, players cannot see every move.
e.zh: 在盲棋变体kriegspiel中，玩家看不到每一步棋。

e.en: The old coat was trimmed with {krimmer}.
e.zh: 那件旧大衣用克里米亚羔皮织物作镶边。

e.en: She identified the collar as {krimmer}.
e.zh: 她认出这个衣领是克里米亚羔皮材质。

e.en: The paper mentioned {krinin} as a plant alkaloid.
e.zh: 论文提到krinin是一种植物生物碱。

e.en: Researchers tested {krinin} in a small laboratory study.
e.zh: 研究人员在一项小型实验室研究中测试了krinin。

e.en: The museum displayed blue crystals of {kroehnkite}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了蓝色的克伦克石晶体。

e.en: Miners found {kroehnkite} in the desert deposit.
e.zh: 矿工在沙漠矿床中发现了克伦克石。

e.en: She learned the {koto} from her grandmother.
e.zh: 她跟祖母学习日本古筝。

e.en: A soft {koto} melody filled the room.
e.zh: 柔和的日本古筝旋律充满了房间。

e.en: The defeated official had to {kotow} before the emperor.
e.zh: 战败的官员不得不在皇帝面前叩头。

e.en: She refused to {kotow} to every powerful donor.
e.zh: 她拒绝对每个有权势的捐助者卑躬屈膝。

e.en: The envoys {kotowed} as the court ceremony began.
e.zh: 宫廷仪式开始时，使节们叩头行礼。

e.en: He never {kotowed} to fashionable opinion.
e.zh: 他从不向流行观点卑躬屈膝。

e.en: The petitioners were {kotowing} outside the palace gate.
e.zh: 请愿者正在宫门外叩头。

e.en: Critics accused the editor of {kotowing} to advertisers.
e.zh: 批评者指责那位编辑向广告商卑躬屈膝。

e.en: In the old ritual, each minister {kotows} three times.
e.zh: 在旧礼仪中，每位大臣都要叩头三次。

e.en: The company {kotows} whenever a celebrity complains.
e.zh: 每当名人抱怨时，这家公司就卑躬屈膝。

e.en: The {kotwal} questioned travelers at the city gate.
e.zh: 那位印度旧时警察长在城门盘问旅人。

e.en: A village elder complained directly to the {kotwal}.
e.zh: 一位村中长老直接向警察长投诉。

e.en: The suspect was taken to the {kotwali} after midnight.
e.zh: 嫌疑人在午夜后被带到警署。

e.en: Merchants gathered outside the {kotwali} to report the theft.
e.zh: 商人们聚集在警察局外报告盗窃案。

e.en: The herders offered us bowls of {koumis}.
e.zh: 牧民端给我们几碗马奶酒。

e.en: Traditional {koumis} has a sharp, fermented taste.
e.zh: 传统马奶酒带有浓烈的发酵味。

e.en: He tasted {koumiss} during his journey across the steppe.
e.zh: 他穿越草原时尝了马奶酒。

e.en: The guide said fresh {koumiss} was mildly alcoholic.
e.zh: 导游说新鲜马奶酒酒精度很低。

e.en: Old travel books often spell the drink {koumyss}.
e.zh: 旧旅行书常把这种饮料拼作koumyss。

e.en: They served chilled {koumyss} in wooden cups.
e.zh: 他们用木杯端上冰镇马奶酒。

e.en: The museum displayed a marble {kouros} near the entrance.
e.zh: 博物馆在入口附近展出了一尊大理石古希腊青年裸像。

e.en: Art students sketched the rigid pose of the {kouros}.
e.zh: 美术学生临摹那尊青年裸像僵直的姿态。

e.en: The engineer recommended {krarupization} for the cable.
e.zh: 工程师建议对电缆进行克拉鲁普化处理。

e.en: Early telephone lines sometimes used {krarupization} to reduce distortion.
e.zh: 早期电话线路有时采用克拉鲁普化处理来减少失真。

e.en: They planned to {krarupize} the long submarine cable.
e.zh: 他们计划对那条很长的海底电缆作克拉鲁普化处理。

e.en: The old manual explains how to {krarupize} a transmission line.
e.zh: 那本旧手册说明了如何对传输线进行克拉鲁普化。

e.en: The supplement contains {kreatin} for muscle recovery.
e.zh: 这种补剂含有肌酸，用于帮助肌肉恢复。

e.en: Some older texts spell creatine as {kreatin}.
e.zh: 一些较旧的文献把creatine拼作kreatin。

e.en: The assay used {kreatinase} to measure creatine levels.
e.zh: 这项检测使用肌酸酶来测量肌酸水平。

e.en: Researchers purified {kreatinase} from a bacterial culture.
e.zh: 研究人员从细菌培养物中纯化出肌酸酶。

e.en: The blood test showed high {kreatinin} levels.
e.zh: 血液检查显示肌酐水平偏高。

e.en: Older medical papers may spell creatinine as {kreatinin}.
e.zh: 较早的医学论文可能把creatinine拼作kreatinin。

e.en: A veteran {kremlinologist} analyzed the leadership reshuffle.
e.zh: 一位资深苏俄政治研究专家分析了领导层改组。

e.en: The newspaper quoted a {kremlinologist} on Moscow's signals.
e.zh: 报纸引用了一名苏俄政治研究专家对莫斯科信号的解读。

e.en: During the Cold War, {kremlinology} shaped many forecasts.
e.zh: 冷战期间，苏俄政治研究影响了许多预测。

e.en: Modern {kremlinology} often reads small changes in official language.
e.zh: 现代苏俄政治研究常从官方措辞的细微变化中解读信息。

e.en: The vein contained visible grains of {krennerite}.
e.zh: 这条矿脉中含有肉眼可见的针碲金银矿颗粒。

e.en: Collectors prize {krennerite} for its rare metallic crystals.
e.zh: 收藏者因其稀有的金属晶体而看重针碲金银矿。

e.en: The doctor mentioned {kreoform} in an old pharmacology lecture.
e.zh: 医生在一堂旧药理学课上提到了克里奥仿。

e.en: A bottle labeled {kreoform} stood in the antique pharmacy case.
e.zh: 古董药柜里放着一瓶标有克里奥仿的药瓶。

e.en: The chemist identified {kreosol} in the wood-tar sample.
e.zh: 化学家在木焦油样品中鉴定出木馏油酚。

e.en: Small amounts of {kreosol} can affect the odor of smoke.
e.zh: 少量木馏油酚会影响烟味。

e.en: The railway ties were treated with {kreosote}.
e.zh: 这些铁路枕木经过杂酚油处理。

e.en: A sharp smell of {kreosote} came from the old fence.
e.zh: 旧篱笆散发出刺鼻的木馏油气味。

e.en: The paper described {kreotoxin} as a suspected toxic compound.
e.zh: 论文把克里奥毒素描述为一种疑似有毒化合物。

e.en: Few laboratories still test for {kreotoxin} today.
e.zh: 如今仍检测克里奥毒素的实验室已经很少。

e.en: The symptoms were once attributed to {kreotoxism}.
e.zh: 这些症状一度被归因于克里奥毒素中毒。

e.en: The textbook lists {kreotoxism} among obsolete poisoning terms.
e.zh: 这本教材把克里奥毒素中毒列为过时的中毒术语之一。

e.en: Grandma served chicken soup with {kreplach}.
e.zh: 奶奶端上了配有犹太馄饨的鸡汤。

e.en: The deli sells potato {kreplach} on Fridays.
e.zh: 这家熟食店每周五出售土豆馅的犹太馄饨。

e.en: The synthesis produced a trace of {kresamine}.
e.zh: 这次合成产生了微量甲酚胺。

e.en: An old chemical catalog listed {kresamine} with related amines.
e.zh: 一本旧化学目录把甲酚胺与相关胺类列在一起。

e.en: The prescription used {kresatin}, a name rarely seen now.
e.zh: 这张处方用了克雷萨汀这个如今很少见的药名。

e.en: Pharmacists found {kresatin} in a nineteenth-century formulary.
e.zh: 药剂师在一本十九世纪处方集中发现了克雷萨汀。

e.en: He lit a {kretek} outside the cafe.
e.zh: 他在咖啡馆外点了一支丁香烟。

e.en: The sweet smell came from Indonesian {kretek} cigarettes.
e.zh: 那股甜香来自印尼丁香烟。

e.en: The dancer performed {krump} with fierce energy.
e.zh: 那名舞者以强烈的力量表演克朗普舞。

e.en: She learned {krumping} in a community dance class.
e.zh: 她在社区舞蹈课上学会了跳克朗普舞。

e.en: The lab used {kryoscopy} to estimate the solution's concentration.
e.zh: 实验室用冰点测定法估算溶液浓度。

e.en: Older chemistry texts sometimes spell cryoscopy as {kryoscopy}.
e.zh: 较旧的化学书有时把cryoscopy拼作kryoscopy。

e.en: In the comic, {kryptonite} weakens Superman.
e.zh: 在漫画里，氪石会削弱超人的力量。

e.en: Chocolate cake is my {kryptonite} when I am dieting.
e.zh: 我节食时，巧克力蛋糕就是我的致命弱点。

e.en: The report measured {kryptopyrrole} levels in urine samples.
e.zh: 报告测量了尿样中的隐吡咯水平。

e.en: Some alternative clinics discuss {kryptopyrrole} in relation to mood symptoms.
e.zh: 一些替代疗法诊所会把隐吡咯与情绪症状联系起来讨论。

e.en: The chemist identified {kryptosterol} in the plant extract.
e.zh: 化学家在植物提取物中鉴定出隐甾醇。

e.en: Few students encounter {kryptosterol} outside specialist biochemistry papers.
e.zh: 很少有学生会在专业生物化学论文之外遇到隐甾醇这个词。

e.en: Papaya contains {kryptoxanthin}, a natural carotenoid pigment.
e.zh: 木瓜含有隐黄质，这是一种天然类胡萝卜素色素。

e.en: The article used the older spelling {kryptoxanthin}.
e.zh: 那篇文章使用了kryptoxanthin这个较旧拼法。

e.en: A {krytron} can switch very high voltages quickly.
e.zh: 冷阴极触发管能快速切换很高的电压。

e.en: The engineer replaced the old {krytron} in the test circuit.
e.zh: 工程师更换了测试电路中的旧冷阴极触发管。

e.en: The museum label identified the mineral as {kryzhanovskite}.
e.zh: 博物馆标签把这种矿物标为克里扎诺夫斯基石。

e.en: Collectors rarely find clear crystals of {kryzhanovskite}.
e.zh: 收藏者很少能找到清晰的克里扎诺夫斯基石晶体。

kuai.t: 块，人民币元的口语说法

e.en: The snack cost only five {kuai}.
e.zh: 这份小吃只花了五块钱。

e.en: He paid thirty {kuai} for the taxi ride.
e.zh: 他坐出租车付了三十块钱。

e.en: She baked a plum {kuchen} for the party.
e.zh: 她为聚会烤了一个李子德式蛋糕。

e.en: The bakery sells cinnamon {kuchen} on weekends.
e.zh: 这家面包店周末卖肉桂德式糕点。

e.en: We bought colorful {kue} at the morning market.
e.zh: 我们在早市买了色彩鲜艳的印尼小糕点。

e.en: Her grandmother served steamed {kue} with tea.
e.zh: 她奶奶端出蒸制小糕点配茶。

e.en: The officer snapped the {kuffs} onto the suspect.
e.zh: 警官把手铐扣在嫌疑人手上。

e.en: His jacket had frayed {kuffs} after years of wear.
e.zh: 他的夹克穿了多年，袖口已经磨破。

e.en: The old soldier carried a curved {kukri}.
e.zh: 那名老兵带着一把弯曲的廓尔喀刀。

e.en: A ceremonial {kukri} hung above the fireplace.
e.zh: 一把仪式用廓尔喀弯刀挂在壁炉上方。

e.en: She served spinach {kuku} with yogurt.
e.zh: 她端上菠菜伊朗蛋饼，旁边配着酸奶。

e.en: The herb {kuku} tasted fresh and light.
e.zh: 这道香草蛋饼吃起来清新爽口。

e.en: A {kulan} can survive in dry steppe regions.
e.zh: 亚洲野驴能在干旱草原地区生存。

e.en: The reserve protects the endangered {kulan}.
e.zh: 这个保护区保护濒危的亚洲野驴。

e.en: We ordered pistachio {kulfi} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后我们点了开心果味印度冰淇淋。

e.en: The {kulfi} was denser than ordinary ice cream.
e.zh: 这种印度冰淇淋比普通冰淇淋更浓稠。

e.en: The historian described Bismarck's {Kulturkampf} in detail.
e.zh: 历史学家详细描述了俾斯麦时期的文化斗争。

e.en: The school debate became a small {kulturkampf}.
e.zh: 这场学校争论演变成一场小型文化冲突。

e.en: Roasted {kumara} is common in New Zealand meals.
e.zh: 烤新西兰甘薯在当地餐食中很常见。

e.en: She mashed the {kumara} with butter.
e.zh: 她把新西兰甘薯加黄油捣成泥。

e.en: He turned the {kumbaloi} slowly in his hand.
e.zh: 他在手里慢慢转动那串希腊消遣珠。

e.en: A silver {kumbaloi} lay on the cafe table.
e.zh: 一串银色希腊念珠放在咖啡馆桌上。

e.en: The meeting ended with a forced {kumbaya} moment.
e.zh: 会议最后出现了一段勉强装和气的场面。

e.en: Critics dismissed the plan as pure {kumbaya}.
e.zh: 批评者把这个计划贬为一味天真的和解姿态。

kuranomycin.t: 一种抗生素物质或化合物

e.en: The lab report mentioned {kuranomycin} as a possible antibiotic compound.
e.zh: 实验室报告提到kuranomycin可能是一种抗生素化合物。

e.en: Researchers tested {kuranomycin} against several bacterial strains.
e.zh: 研究人员用kuranomycin测试了几种细菌菌株。

e.en: The extract contained traces of {kurchamine} and related alkaloids.
e.zh: 这种提取物含有微量kurchamine及相关生物碱。

e.en: Chemists isolated {kurchamine} from the bark sample.
e.zh: 化学家从树皮样本中分离出了kurchamine。

e.en: Older chemistry books sometimes used {kurchatovium} for element 104.
e.zh: 旧版化学书有时用kurchatovium指104号元素。

e.en: The name {kurchatovium} was later replaced in official usage.
e.zh: kurchatovium这个名称后来在正式用法中被取代。

e.en: The healer prepared {kurchi} bark as a traditional remedy.
e.zh: 这位医者把止痢木树皮制成传统药方。

e.en: {Kurchi} is known for its bitter medicinal bark.
e.zh: 止痢木以其苦味的药用树皮而闻名。

kurchine.t: 止痢木中的一种生物碱

e.en: The study measured {kurchine} in the herbal preparation.
e.zh: 这项研究测定了草药制剂中的kurchine含量。

e.en: {Kurchine} was listed among the plant's active alkaloids.
e.zh: kurchine被列为该植物的活性生物碱之一。

e.en: The old text described a small {kurf} beyond the hills.
e.zh: 那篇古文描写了山那边的一个小村落。

e.en: Travelers rested in the {kurf} before crossing the pass.
e.zh: 旅人们在村子里休息后才翻越山口。

e.en: Archaeologists opened a {kurgan} on the steppe.
e.zh: 考古学家在草原上发掘了一座库尔干墓。

e.en: The ancient {kurgan} held weapons, pottery, and bones.
e.zh: 那座古代坟冢中有武器、陶器和遗骨。

e.en: The scandal revealed a hidden {kuromaku} behind the minister.
e.zh: 这起丑闻揭露了部长背后的幕后黑手。

e.en: Reporters searched for the {kuromaku} controlling the deal.
e.zh: 记者们寻找操纵这笔交易的幕后人物。

e.en: The resin sample contained {kuromatsuol} and several terpenes.
e.zh: 树脂样本中含有kuromatsuol和几种萜类物质。

e.en: Scientists identified {kuromatsuol} in the pine extract.
e.zh: 科学家在松树提取物中鉴定出了kuromatsuol。

e.en: A tall {kurrajong} shaded the edge of the paddock.
e.zh: 一棵高大的澳洲瓶树给牧场边缘投下阴影。

e.en: They twisted {kurrajong} fiber into a rough cord.
e.zh: 他们把澳洲瓶树纤维搓成一根粗绳。

e.en: The soup was flavored with chopped {kurrat}.
e.zh: 这道汤用切碎的埃及韭调味。

e.en: Farmers grow {kurrat} much like ordinary leeks.
e.zh: 农民种植埃及韭的方式很像种普通韭葱。

e.en: Doctors studied {kuru} as a rare prion disease.
e.zh: 医生把库鲁病作为一种罕见朊病毒病来研究。

e.en: The history of {kuru} changed ideas about infectious proteins.
e.zh: 库鲁病的历史改变了人们对感染性蛋白的认识。

kurus.t: 库鲁什；旧土耳其货币单位

e.en: The coin was worth fifty {kurus} in old currency.
e.zh: 这枚硬币在旧币制中值五十库鲁什。

e.en: He paid a few {kurus} for bread at the market.
e.zh: 他在市场上花了几个库鲁什买面包。

e.en: The aquarium displayed a small {kusafugu} from Japan.
e.zh: 水族馆展出了一条来自日本的小草河豚。

e.en: Chefs avoid serving {kusafugu} unless it is prepared safely.
e.zh: 厨师只有在能安全处理时才会供应草河豚。

e.en: The zoo kept a dwarf {kusimanse} in a warm enclosure.
e.zh: 动物园把一只侏儒库西曼斯獴养在温暖的围栏里。

e.en: A {kusimanse} forages quickly through leaves and soil.
e.zh: 库西曼斯獴会在落叶和泥土中快速觅食。

e.en: The meal cost five hundred {kwanza}.
e.zh: 这顿饭花了五百宽扎。

e.en: Prices were listed in {kwanza} at the market.
e.zh: 市场里的价格都用宽扎标出。

kwashiorkor.t: 夸希奥科病；蛋白质缺乏症

e.en: The clinic treated children with {kwashiorkor}.
e.zh: 诊所治疗患有夸希奥科病的儿童。

e.en: Severe protein deficiency can cause {kwashiorkor}.
e.zh: 严重缺乏蛋白质会导致夸希奥科病。

kwela.t: 奎拉音乐；南非街头音乐

e.en: The band played lively {kwela} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后乐队演奏了欢快的奎拉音乐。

e.en: She collected old {kwela} records from Johannesburg.
e.zh: 她收藏来自约翰内斯堡的老奎拉唱片。

e.en: He paddled the {kyack} across the lake.
e.zh: 他划着皮艇穿过湖面。

e.en: The old {kyack} leaked near the stern.
e.zh: 那艘旧皮艇在船尾附近漏水。

e.en: They loaded the {kyak} onto the roof rack.
e.zh: 他们把皮艇装到车顶架上。

e.en: A narrow {kyak} moved silently downstream.
e.zh: 一艘狭长的皮艇静静顺流而下。

kyanite.t: 蓝晶石；蓝色硅酸盐矿物

e.en: The pendant contained a shard of {kyanite}.
e.zh: 吊坠里嵌着一片蓝晶石。

e.en: Geologists found {kyanite} in the metamorphic rock.
e.zh: 地质学家在变质岩中发现了蓝晶石。

e.en: The fence posts were {kyanized} before installation.
e.zh: 篱笆柱在安装前经过氯化汞防腐处理。

e.en: Old manuals describe {kyanized} timber for damp sites.
e.zh: 旧手册提到潮湿地段可用经氯化汞处理的木材。

kyanizing.t: 用氯化汞处理木材防腐

e.en: The company specialized in {kyanizing} railway sleepers.
e.zh: 这家公司专门用氯化汞处理铁路枕木以防腐。

e.en: {Kyanizing} reduced decay in exposed timber.
e.zh: 用氯化汞防腐处理能减少外露木材腐烂。

e.en: The dye maker once called aniline {kyanol}.
e.zh: 染料制造商曾把苯胺称作蓝油。

e.en: A chemistry text listed {kyanol} among old trade names.
e.zh: 一本化学教材把蓝油列入旧商品名。

e.en: The taxi fare was eight thousand {kyat}.
e.zh: 出租车费是八千缅元。

e.en: She exchanged dollars for {kyat} at the bank.
e.zh: 她在银行把美元兑换成缅元。

e.en: Early computer scientists studied {kybernetics}.
e.zh: 早期计算机科学家研究控制论。

e.en: His essay linked politics with {kybernetics}.
e.zh: 他的文章把政治与控制论联系起来。

kyley.t: 回力镖；澳洲土著投掷棒

e.en: The museum displayed a wooden {kyley}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一根木制回力镖。

e.en: He explained how a {kyley} returns when thrown correctly.
e.zh: 他解释了回力镖正确投掷后如何飞回。

e.en: A carved {kylin} guarded the temple gate.
e.zh: 一尊雕刻的麒麟守在寺门旁。

e.en: The robe was embroidered with a golden {kylin}.
e.zh: 那件袍子绣着一只金色麒麟。

kylinone.t: 麒麟酮；一种化学化合物

e.en: The paper reported traces of {kylinone} in the extract.
e.zh: 论文报告提取物中含有微量麒麟酮。

e.en: Researchers isolated {kylinone} during the analysis.
e.zh: 研究人员在分析过程中分离出了麒麟酮。

e.en: The archaeologist cleaned a painted {kylix}.
e.zh: 考古学家清理了一只彩绘的古希腊浅酒杯。

e.en: Wine was served in a shallow {kylix}.
e.zh: 酒盛在一只浅浅的古希腊酒杯里。

e.en: The surgeon described the case as {kyllopodia}.
e.zh: 外科医生把这个病例描述为弯足畸形。

e.en: Medical notes recorded congenital {kyllopodia} in the infant.
e.zh: 病历记录该婴儿有先天性弯足畸形。

e.en: The nomads offered us bowls of {kumis}.
e.zh: 游牧民给我们端来了几碗马奶酒。

e.en: Traditional {kumis} is made from fermented mare's milk.
e.zh: 传统马奶酒是用发酵的母马奶制成的。

e.en: He tasted {kumiss} during his trip across the steppe.
e.zh: 他穿越草原旅行时尝了马奶酒。

e.en: The sour smell of {kumiss} filled the tent.
e.zh: 马奶酒的酸味弥漫在帐篷里。

e.en: She won the final {kumite} match.
e.zh: 她赢得了最后的空手道对打比赛。

e.en: In {kumite}, timing matters as much as power.
e.zh: 在空手道对打中，时机和力量同样重要。

e.en: She placed {kumkum} on her forehead before the ceremony.
e.zh: 仪式前，她在额头上点了印度红粉。

e.en: A small box of {kumkum} sat near the shrine.
e.zh: 神龛旁放着一小盒额饰红粉。

e.en: After dinner, he served chilled {kummel}.
e.zh: 晚饭后，他端上了冰镇的小茴香利口酒。

e.en: The {kummel} had a strong caraway flavor.
e.zh: 这种小茴香利口酒有浓重的葛缕子味。

e.en: He wore a black {kummerbund} with his tuxedo.
e.zh: 他穿燕尾服时系了一条黑色礼服腰封。

e.en: The old portrait showed a soldier in a red {kummerbund}.
e.zh: 那幅旧肖像里，一名士兵系着红色宽腰带。

e.en: The fishermen loaded rice onto the {kumpit}.
e.zh: 渔民把大米装上那艘菲律宾小船。

e.en: A wooden {kumpit} carried goods between the islands.
e.zh: 一艘木制货船在岛屿之间运送货物。

e.en: Guests were welcomed with cups of {kumys}.
e.zh: 客人们受到欢迎时喝到了几杯马奶酒。

e.en: Fresh {kumys} tastes lightly sour and fizzy.
e.zh: 新鲜马奶酒味道微酸，还带一点气泡感。

e.en: The traveler described {kumyss} in his diary.
e.zh: 那位旅行者在日记中描述了马奶酒。

e.en: They fermented mare's milk to make {kumyss}.
e.zh: 他们发酵母马奶来制作马奶酒。

e.en: The ancient text mentions a giant {kun}.
e.zh: 这部古籍提到了一条传说中的巨大鲲。

e.en: In the story, the {kun} changes into a bird.
e.zh: 在这个故事里，鲲变成了一只鸟。

e.en: The museum ticket cost twenty {kuna}.
e.zh: 博物馆门票价格是二十库纳。

e.en: Croatia used the {kuna} before adopting the euro.
e.zh: 克罗地亚在采用欧元之前使用库纳。

e.en: He learned {kungfu} from his grandfather.
e.zh: 他跟祖父学习功夫。

e.en: The film made {kungfu} popular overseas.
e.zh: 这部电影让中国功夫在海外流行起来。

e.en: Her ring held a pale pink {kunzite}.
e.zh: 她的戒指上镶着一颗淡粉色的孔赛石。

e.en: Collectors value clear {kunzite} for its delicate color.
e.zh: 收藏者看重透明锂辉石宝石的柔和色泽。

e.en: The chemist added {kupferron} to the solution.
e.zh: 化学家向溶液中加入了铜铁试剂。

e.en: Older methods used {kupferron} to separate metal ions.
e.zh: 较早的方法用铜铁试剂分离金属离子。

e.en: The collector labeled the gray crystal as {kuskite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把这块灰色晶体标为硫砷铅矿。

e.en: A thin vein of {kuskite} appeared in the ore sample.
e.zh: 矿石样本中出现了一条细细的硫砷铅矿脉。

e.en: The old remedy used powdered {kusso} for tapeworms.
e.zh: 这种老方子用苦苏花粉来治绦虫。

e.en: She found dried {kusso} listed in a nineteenth-century pharmacopoeia.
e.zh: 她在一本十九世纪药典里看到了干苦苏花。

e.en: The pinkish carbonate was identified as {kutnahorite}.
e.zh: 这种略带粉色的碳酸盐被鉴定为锰白云石。

e.en: Geologists found {kutnahorite} beside the manganese ore.
e.zh: 地质学家在锰矿旁发现了锰白云石。

e.en: He ordered cold {kvass} with his lunch.
e.zh: 他午餐时点了一杯冰格瓦斯。

e.en: Traditional {kvass} is made from fermented rye bread.
e.zh: 传统格瓦斯是用发酵黑麦面包制成的。

e.en: Grandparents often {kvell} over every new photo.
e.zh: 祖父母常常看着每张新照片都喜不自禁地夸赞。

e.en: She began to {kvell} when her son won the prize.
e.zh: 儿子获奖时，她忍不住得意地夸了起来。

e.en: Please stop and {kvetch} about the service later.
e.zh: 请先别抱怨服务，晚点再说。

e.en: Everyone knew him as a harmless old {kvetch}.
e.zh: 大家都知道他是个无伤大雅的老牢骚鬼。

e.en: She {kvetched} about the noisy hotel all morning.
e.zh: 她整个上午都在抱怨那家酒店太吵。

e.en: The customers {kvetched} until the manager apologized.
e.zh: 顾客们一直发牢骚，直到经理道歉。

e.en: No one wanted to sit beside the office {kvetcher}.
e.zh: 没人想坐在办公室那个爱抱怨的人旁边。

e.en: He sounds like a {kvetcher}, but his complaints are fair.
e.zh: 他听起来像个牢骚鬼，但他的抱怨是有道理的。

e.en: She {kvetches} whenever the train is late.
e.zh: 火车一晚点，她就会抱怨。

e.en: His daily {kvetches} filled the family chat.
e.zh: 他每天的牢骚话塞满了家庭群聊。

e.en: They spent dinner {kvetching} about rising prices.
e.zh: 他们吃晚饭时一直在抱怨物价上涨。

e.en: Her constant {kvetching} made the meeting feel longer.
e.zh: 她不停发牢骚，让会议显得更漫长。

e.en: The early {kvutza} shared tools and meals.
e.zh: 早期的集体农庄小组共用工具，也一起吃饭。

e.en: He studied how a {kvutza} differed from a kibbutz.
e.zh: 他研究集体农庄小组与基布兹有何不同。

e.en: The taxi ride cost fifty {kwacha}.
e.zh: 这趟出租车花了五十克瓦查。

e.en: Inflation weakened the {kwacha} against the dollar.
e.zh: 通货膨胀削弱了克瓦查兑美元的汇率。

e.en: The party shifted to {kwaito} after midnight.
e.zh: 午夜过后，派对音乐换成了南非快活托。

e.en: Her documentary traces {kwaito} from township clubs.
e.zh: 她的纪录片追溯快活托音乐在城镇俱乐部中的起源。

e.en: A shaggy {kyloe} stood near the stone wall.
e.zh: 一头毛茸茸的苏格兰高地牛站在石墙旁。

e.en: The old farmer preferred hardy {kyloes} for the windy hills.
e.zh: 那位老农更喜欢能适应多风丘陵的高地牛。

e.en: The physiologist studied the {kymogram} after the experiment.
e.zh: 生理学家在实验后研究了这张波动记录图。

e.en: A clear {kymogram} showed each change in pressure.
e.zh: 清晰的波动记录图显示了每一次压力变化。

e.en: The lab used a {kymographic} method to record muscle movement.
e.zh: 实验室用波动记录仪方法记录肌肉运动。

e.en: Old {kymographic} traces can still be useful to historians of medicine.
e.zh: 旧的波动记录仪曲线对医学史研究者仍有用。

e.en: The specialist mentioned {kymokinoscopy} during the eye examination.
e.zh: 专科医生在眼部检查中提到了眼动描记检查法。

e.en: Few clinics still teach {kymokinoscopy} as a routine technique.
e.zh: 如今很少有诊所仍把眼动描记检查法作为常规技术来教。

e.en: The poem speaks of {kyne} grazing in the meadow.
e.zh: 这首诗写到牛群在草地上吃草。

e.en: In older English, {kyne} could mean cattle.
e.zh: 在较古老的英语中，kyne 可以表示牛类。

e.en: Severe {kyphoscoliosis} can affect breathing.
e.zh: 严重的脊柱后侧凸可能影响呼吸。

e.en: The surgeon reviewed the child's {kyphoscoliosis} on the scan.
e.zh: 外科医生查看了扫描片上孩子的脊柱后侧凸情况。

e.en: Mild {kyphosis} may cause no pain at all.
e.zh: 轻度脊柱后凸可能完全不会疼痛。

e.en: Exercises helped improve her posture after {kyphosis} was diagnosed.
e.zh: 确诊脊柱后凸后，锻炼帮助她改善了姿势。

e.en: The choir sang the {Kyrie} before the sermon.
e.zh: 唱诗班在布道前唱了《垂怜经》。

e.en: A quiet {kyrie} echoed through the chapel.
e.zh: 一段低声的求主怜悯祷词在小礼拜堂回荡。

e.en: The chemist used {kyroscopy} to estimate the solute's molecular weight.
e.zh: 化学家用冷冻点测定法估算溶质的分子量。

e.en: In the lecture, {kyroscopy} was compared with boiling-point methods.
e.zh: 讲座中，冷冻点测定法被拿来与沸点法比较。

e.en: The doctor adjusted the {kyrtometer} against the patient's spine.
e.zh: 医生把胸背弯曲测量器贴着病人的脊柱调好。

e.en: An old {kyrtometer} lay in the medical museum case.
e.zh: 一台旧的胸背弯曲测量器放在医学博物馆的展柜里。

e.en: Old letters {kythe} a gentler side of him.
e.zh: 旧信显露出他更温和的一面。

e.en: The legend says the spirit will {kythe} at dusk.
e.zh: 传说那灵魂会在黄昏时显现。

e.en: Her kindness {kythed} itself in small acts.
e.zh: 她的善意通过一些小举动显现出来。

e.en: The truth had {kythed} before anyone spoke.
e.zh: 还没等人开口，真相已经显露了。

e.en: The hero's courage was {kything} in every choice.
e.zh: 英雄的勇气在每个选择中都显现出来。

e.en: They spoke of {kything} the message through ritual.
e.zh: 他们谈到通过仪式来显明这条信息。

e.en: The weather team launched a {kytoon} before sunrise.
e.zh: 气象小组在日出前放飞了一个风筝气球。

e.en: A tethered {kytoon} carried the small camera above the field.
e.zh: 一个系留风筝气球把小相机带到田野上方。

e.en: She reached fifth {kyu} after months of judo practice.
e.zh: 练了几个月柔道后，她达到了五级。

e.en: Beginners usually hold a {kyu} rank before earning dan status.
e.zh: 初学者通常先有级位，之后才取得段位。

e.en: He practices {kyudo} every Saturday morning.
e.zh: 他每周六早上练习日本弓道。

e.en: In {kyudo}, posture matters as much as hitting the target.
e.zh: 在日本弓道中，姿势和命中靶心同样重要。
